item.title: Pope Leo to hold Wednesday audience for first time since cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo will hold a general audience with pilgrims at the Vatican on Wednesday for the first time since undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the Vatican said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo will hold a general audience with pilgrims at the Vatican on Wednesday for the first time since undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the Vatican said. The 71-year-old pontiff had [USN:L1N45Z08S TEXT:"an operation"] on October 13 to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, fuelling speculation about how his illness might change his 17-month papacy. Leo pledged on Sunday, in his first public event since the surgery, that he would slowly resume his usual activities as the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics. The pope hosts a general audience with pilgrims on most Wednesdays of the year. It is either held in St. Peter's Square or indoors, depending on the weather.

item.title: MSCI's case against Indonesian stocks and the $65 billion fallout
item.description: Global index provider MSCI said last week it was considering downgrading Indonesia's stock market to "standalone" status from "emerging market", sparking a selloff that wiped about $65 billion in market value on the day of the announcement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Global index provider MSCI [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"said"] last week it was considering downgrading Indonesia's stock market to "standalone" status from "emerging market", sparking a selloff that wiped about $65 billion in market value on the day of the announcement. The announcement is the [USN:L1N46500W TEXT:"latest setback"] for Indonesian markets this year, after MSCI first flagged concerns in January over the investability of Indonesian equities. Jakarta responded by promising a raft of reforms to address those concerns. WHAT ARE MSCI'S CONCERNS? MSCI said last week that Jakarta had failed to make "sufficient progress" in demonstrating consistent implementation of market reforms and their sustained impact while weak enforcement remained a concern. The index provider said in January its clients flagged problems around market data that obscured what proportion of Indonesian companies' shares could be freely traded and how the exchange categorised stock owners. MSCI said its clients pointed to opaque shareholding structures and coordinated trading behaviour that undermined "proper price formation," suggesting prices of some Indonesian equities were being artificially supported, which raised questions about transparency, oversight and governance. That meant Indonesia did not meet the [USN:L6N46208E TEXT:"requirements and standards"] of markets listed in the "emerging market" category, and could be downgraded to "frontier market." WHAT HAS INDONESIA DONE SINCE THEN? MSCI's initial warning in January led to [USN:L1N3YV02G TEXT:"mass resignations"] of top officials, who were replaced by figures widely known and trusted by markets. Indonesia's financial regulator (OJK) then [USN:L1N40J0E0 TEXT:"doubled"] the free float rule for listed firms to 15% from 7.5%, introduced tighter disclosure requirements for shareholders with at least [USN:L1N3Z70D2 TEXT:"a 1% holding"] and expanded the classification of shareholder types. Minimum capital rules for securities firms and certain asset managers [USN:L4N40Z0CW TEXT:"were also tightened"] to reduce the risk of market manipulation. The stock exchange (IDX) released [USN:L1N40L06Z TEXT:"a list"] of stocks with high shareholder concentrations in April, in moves intended to shed light on potential coordinated trading. Despite those moves, MSCI extended its review of Indonesia from June to November. A spate of fresh moves followed. IDX said it would add [USN:L1N43G0DO TEXT:"37 stocks"] to its list of companies with highly concentrated shareholdings, and in early October, it would adopt more reforms such as changing initial public offering [USN:L6N45W007 TEXT:"rules"] by scrapping a minimum share price requirement to make shares more affordable and fundraising easier, in line with the earlier [USN:L1N44H08T TEXT:"removal"] of a floor price for shares. However, MSCI announced last week - a month before its scheduled review - that it was initiating a process to move Indonesia even lower than "frontier market" - that is, to "standalone" status. WHAT IS INDONESIA DOING NOW? Despite the announced reforms, MSCI said significant concerns remain around market dysfunction, including continued suspected coordinated trading behaviour and lack of evidence of meaningful enforcement. Hours after MSCI's announcement last week, OJK handed down a total of 2.1 trillion rupiah ($116.41 million) [USN:L6N4620JP TEXT:"in fines"] against entities involved in the trading of three companies' shares. The fines were linked to market manipulation practices. Beyond the fines, Indonesian authorities have also got the police involved to investigate "alleged violations or criminal acts in the capital market." The police chief has promised "firm action" to ensure legal certainty in the capital market. Authorities in Jakarta say they will speak to MSCI to clarify its concerns, which they say came as a shock. Jakarta has until April 30, 2027, to assuage MSCI's concerns and prevent a market reclassification. MSCI will announce its decision on or before June 30. Meanwhile, to stem the selloff, IDX [USN:L6N46501N TEXT:"cut"] the exchange's daily limit for stock price declines to 7% from 15% to curb market volatility. WHY IS MSCI CRITICAL FOR INDONESIA? A shift to "standalone" status would risk cutting [USN:L6N46202Y TEXT:"Southeast Asia's biggest economy"] off from international capital, relegating it to an investment backwater and clubbing it with a group of [USN:L6N46208E TEXT:"standalone"] markets that includes Lebanon and Zimbabwe. The drop to "standalone" status would further pressure Indonesia's economy as the market lost about $60 billion on Friday alone, following MSCI's recent announcement. That figure shoots up to $350 billion in market valuation wiped out since January. Jakarta's benchmark stocks (.JKSE) fell more than 5% on Monday after plummeting 11.6% on Friday - the highest single-day loss in nearly three decades - making the market the world's [USN:L1N46504M TEXT:"worst"] performer with a more than 40% drop so far this year. The rupiah currency, which has also been under pressure due to a strong US dollar as well as investors' concerns over its fiscal risks, is already the worst-performing currency in the region, falling more than 7% so far this year. ($1 = 18,040.0000 rupiah)

item.title: Uber wins bid to throw out UK mass lawsuit by black cab drivers
item.description: Uber on Monday said it had won its bid to throw out two linked lawsuits valued at around £340 million ($453 million) brought by thousands of London black cab drivers and two former private hire companies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Uber (UBER.N) on Monday said it had won its bid to throw out two linked lawsuits valued at around £340 million ($453 million) brought by thousands of London black cab drivers and two former private hire companies. The ride-hailing app was sued in 2024 over allegations about how it obtained a private hire vehicle operating licence in the British capital, with the claimants alleging Uber gave "misleading and inaccurate information" to Transport for London. Uber denied the allegations and also argued the lawsuits were filed after the six-year limitation period for bringing such a claim, meaning they should be thrown out. A copy of the High Court's ruling was not immediately available.

item.title: Qatar will soon announce local defence production hub, minister of state says
item.description: The Gulf Arab state of Qatar will soon announce a defence production hub, the minister of state for defence affairs told the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Gulf Arab state of Qatar will soon announce a defence production hub, the minister of state for defence affairs told the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday. Against the background of the Middle East conflict , which has drawn Iranian attacks on energy-rich Gulf countries, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said: "We are partnering with a regional partner, in addition to other partners such as the United States, the United Kingdom, France, to make sure either we do local protection or we are investing in some of these companies." When asked about the threats faced by Qatar and the other Gulf countries from ballistic missiles, drones and cyberattacks, Al Thani said: "Soon we are going to announce a new partnership that we will do with the regional partners to establish a new initiative towards building capability into these three elements and others." He did not elaborate. The Iran war has dealt a blow to Qatar. The country was [USN:L1N43W04H TEXT:"forced to shut down"] much of its main LNG complex at Ras Laffan shortly after the start of hostilities and it suffered from restrictions on global shipping through the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Hong Kong regulator sees rise in listing of young growth firms
item.description: Hong Kong has seen an increase in listings of growth companies — those yet to achieve sustained profitability but with strong growth potential — due to improved market infrastructure, the CEO of its Securities and Futures Commission said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hong Kong has seen an increase in listings of growth companies — those yet to achieve sustained profitability but with strong growth potential — due to improved market infrastructure, the CEO of its Securities and Futures Commission said on Monday. Among firms listed on Hong Kong's bourse, the portion of growth companies in sectors like biotechnology and AI has risen to 30% from 10% in 2023, Julia Leung said during a seminar in Tokyo hosted by Japan's Financial Services Agency. "Our stock exchange has actually done proactive reform and put in regimes to attract growth companies," she said at the seminar on global capital markets. That has balanced the need to offer sufficient investor protection, while allowing the entry of firms that have not fully commercialised their products yet, she added. Most growth companies were three to five years old, with some developing AI models. The Hong Kong stock exchange has also improved market infrastructure for clearing and settlement of deals, Leung said. Hong Kong benefits immensely from being on the doorstep of China, which is a big producer of the entire AI chain, she said, adding that startups were hungry for capital and looking for international expansion. "Now we have a very buoyant market," she said. "But it is important, particularly where market conditions are weakening, that we actually be a lot more selective" in what to bring to the market and "prioritise quality over speed," she added. The Securities and Futures Commission is an independent body set up in 1989 to regulate Hong Kong's securities and futures markets.

item.title: ガザの食糧支援プログラム、資金不足で50万人分削減へ＝ＷＦＰ
item.description: [カイロ／ガザ １９日 ロイター] - 国連世界食糧計画（ＷＦＰ）
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[カイロ／ガザ １９日 ロイター] - 国連世界食糧計画（ＷＦＰ） は、資金不足によりパレスチナ自治区ガザでの支援プログラムを大幅に縮小せざるを得なくなっており、約５０万人が毎月の食糧支援を受けられなくなると明らかにした。

毎月の支援の受給者数を１６０万人から１１０万人に減らすという。

また、食糧配給は半減し、７万５０００世帯への現金支援が削減されたほか、自炊ができない人々への１日当たりの温かい食事の提供数は２５万食から１５万食に減少。アクセスが困難な地域の一部世帯では、温かい食事が１日おきにしか提供されなくなっている。

ＷＦＰによると、ガザの人口の３分の２に当たる約１４０万人が危機レベル以上の食料不安に直面しており、そのうち約２０万人は緊急事態に陥っている。

ＷＦＰは、ガザとイスラエル占領下のヨルダン川西岸における重要な活動を維持するため、今後６カ月間で４億５０００万ドルを緊急に必要としていると述べた。

item.title: Bank Indonesia narrowly expected to hold interest rates despite market turmoil
item.description: Indonesia's central bank will hold interest rates steady on Wednesday, according to a narrow majority of economists in a Reuters poll who said the rupiah's slide following a warning Indonesian stocks might be dropped from key global indexes would have little bearing on the policy decision.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Trivedi
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's central bank will hold interest rates steady on Wednesday, according to a narrow majority of economists in a Reuters poll who said the rupiah's slide following a warning Indonesian stocks might be dropped from key global indexes would have little bearing on the policy decision. The currency, down about 8% so far this year, fell nearly 1% after MSCI shocked domestic markets on Friday when it said it was considering moving Indonesia to "standalone" status from the "emerging markets" designation it has held since 1989. The warning prompted some economists to change their forecasts on Friday and Monday from expectations of no rate change on October 21 to a rate hike. Citibank, which expected no move, now forecasts a pre-emptive 50-basis-point increase. But [USN:L1N45N03U TEXT:"prices"] remain broadly contained. Headline inflation was 3.28% in September, within BI's 1.5% to 3.5% target range, while the core measure eased to 2.84%, which may give policymakers confidence to hold rates for now. Slightly more than half of economists polled (15 of 29) from October 13 to 19, expected Bank Indonesia to keep its benchmark 7-day reverse repurchase rate (IDCBRR=ECI) at 5.75% on Wednesday. They also expected it to leave its overnight deposit and lending facility rates unchanged at 4.75% and 6.50%, respectively. Jakarta's benchmark stock index (.JKSE) , already the world's worst performer this year, [USN:L1N46500W TEXT:"fell"] a further 5% in early trading on Monday, after plunging 11.6% on Friday, its worst one-day fall since January 1998 following MSCI's surprise warning. "I think it's far too early to suggest this will matter from a monetary policy perspective ... but obviously Friday's news has complicated things," said Miguel Chanco, chief emerging Asia economist at UK-based Pantheon Macroeconomics. "Barring (this) event...which is a shock to everyone, the fundamentals still don't suggest to me hiking is necessary, especially after Bank Indonesia already hiked by 100 basis points earlier this year." Some economists argued BI could continue relying on non-rate measures to maintain currency stability, including lowering the cost of foreign-exchange hedging with the central bank, encouraging the use of currencies other than the US dollar, and drawing on its $146.3 billion in FX reserves rather than raising rates. But a comfortable majority of economists, 15 of 22, expected the key rate to rise from 5.75% to 6.00% or more before year-end. That [USN:L4N45D00H TEXT:"view"] was held even before the blow from MSCI, reflecting concerns higher oil prices could lift inflation and a hawkish US Federal Reserve would keep pressure on the rupiah. There was no clear consensus among economists on where borrowing costs would go beyond this year. The median forecast showed the policy rate remaining at 6.00% throughout 2027. "At the end of the day, one of their very clear priorities is IDR stability," said Lavanya Venkateswaran, senior ASEAN economist at OCBC Bank, who brought forward a December rate hike forecast to Wednesday. ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

item.title: India's Jio IPO anchor investor quota nearly 30 times oversubscribed, source says
item.description: Mukesh Ambani's $3.2 billion Jio Platforms IPO has drawn bids from institutions including GIC, BlackRock and Fidelity, totaling almost 30 times the quota reserved for anchor investors, a person with direct knowledge said.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra, Vibhuti Sharma
item.content:encoded: Mukesh Ambani's $3.2 billion Jio Platforms IPO has drawn bids from institutions including GIC, BlackRock and Fidelity, totaling almost 30 times the quota reserved for anchor investors, a person with direct knowledge said. The telecoms, cloud and AI group on Monday opened its record initial public offering to institutional investors who can bid for up to 30% of the offering reserved exclusively for them, before the issue opens for public subscription on Wednesday. Jio Platforms is set to raise up to $3.2 billion at a [USN:L1N4600N0 TEXT:"valuation"] of $108.3 billion in what will be India's biggest ever IPO. Fidelity, Singapore's GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock were among the investors to place bids for the institutional quota, the person told Reuters. Reliance, which is the ultimate owner of Jio Platforms, did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. ADIA, BlackRock, Fidelity and GIC did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

item.title: Latin American airlines eye Venezuela return as ties thaw, hurdles remain
item.description: Latin American airlines are showing renewed interest in Venezuela as diplomatic channels reopen and carriers prepare to restore links to Caracas, though industry executives said damaged airport infrastructure and an outdated regulatory framework remain major obstacles to a broader recovery.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: Latin American airlines are showing renewed interest in Venezuela as diplomatic channels reopen and carriers prepare to restore links to Caracas, though industry executives said damaged airport infrastructure and an outdated regulatory framework remain major obstacles to a broader recovery. Venezuela has strong long-term potential because of its location, but the immediate priority is rebuilding the country's aviation platform after the deadly June earthquakes damaged its main international gateway at Maiquetía, outside Caracas, Peter Cerda, head of the Latin American and Caribbean Air Transport Association (ALTA), said in a press conference on Sunday. "I think Venezuela has significant potential. Strategically and geographically, it is in a perfect location. It is a market with major opportunities," Cerda said ALTA has been in constant dialogue with Venezuelan authorities, Cerda said, but emergency recovery efforts have taken precedence over broader policy discussions Chile's LATAM Airlines (LTM.SN) said it was encouraged by the reopening process and by improving diplomatic conditions between Santiago and Caracas LATAM Chief Executive Roberto Alvo stopped short of announcing additional routes, but said LATAM would assess future opportunities as conditions improve "LATAM's interest is to continue connecting South America with itself and with the world... As we see that we can develop our connectivity to Venezuela, we will evaluate those opportunities," Alvo said Cerda said the reopening interest was not limited to one carrier or one market, adding that airlines in the US, Europe and the Middle East were also looking again at Venezuela

item.title: Aerolíneas latinoamericanas evalúan volver a Venezuela ante el deshielo diplomático, pese a obstáculos
item.description: Las aerolíneas latinoamericanas muestran un renovado interés en Venezuela mientras se reabren los canales diplomáticos y las compañías se preparan para restablecer conexiones con Caracas, aunque directivos del sector señalaron que los daños en la infraestructura aeroportuaria y un marco regulatorio desactualizado siguen siendo grandes obstáculos para una recuperación más amplia.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: Las aerolíneas latinoamericanas muestran un renovado interés en Venezuela mientras se reabren los canales diplomáticos y las compañías se preparan para restablecer conexiones con Caracas, aunque directivos del sector señalaron que los daños en la infraestructura aeroportuaria y un marco regulatorio desactualizado siguen siendo grandes obstáculos para una recuperación más amplia. Venezuela tiene un gran potencial a largo plazo por su ubicación, pero la prioridad inmediata es reconstruir la infraestructura aeronáutica del país después de que los mortales terremotos de junio dañaran su principal puerta de entrada internacional, en Maiquetía, a las afueras de Caracas, dijo Peter Cerdá, director ejecutivo de la Asociación Latinoamericana y del Caribe de Transporte Aéreo (ALTA), en una rueda de prensa el domingo. "Yo creo que hay un potencial importante para Venezuela. Estratégicamente, geográficamente está una localización perfecta. Es un mercado que hay grandes oportunidades", afirmó Cerdá. ALTA ha mantenido un diálogo constante con las autoridades venezolanas, dijo Cerdá, pero las labores de recuperación de emergencia han tenido prioridad sobre los debates más amplios en materia de políticas para el sector. La chilena LATAM Airlines (LTM.SN) dijo que veía con optimismo el proceso de reapertura y la mejora de las relaciones diplomáticas entre Santiago y Caracas. El gerente general de LATAM, Roberto Alvo, no llegó a anunciar rutas adicionales, pero dijo que la compañía evaluaría futuras oportunidades a medida que mejoren las condiciones. "El interés de Latam es seguir conectando Sudamérica consigo mismo y con el mundo. (...) En la medida que veamos que podamos desarrollar nuestra conectividad hacia Venezuela, vamos a evaluar esas oportunidades", afirmó Alvo. Cerdá dijo que el interés por retomar las conexiones no se limitaba a una compañía ni a un mercado, y añadió que las aerolíneas de Estados Unidos, Europa y Oriente Medio también estaban volviendo a fijarse en Venezuela.

item.title: What you need to know about the 2026 US midterm elections
item.description: Early voting has been underway for weeks ahead of the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, when US voters will elect members of the House of Representatives and Senate and governors in states across the country.
item.dc:creator: Richard Cowan
item.content:encoded: Early voting has been underway for weeks ahead of the November 3, 2026, midterm elections , when US voters will elect members of the House of Representatives and Senate and governors in states across the country. Held in the middle of each four-year presidential term, the midterms by definition do not involve the president. But for anyone who thinks they lack drama or importance this year, consider these two statistics: More than 100 million people likely will cast ballots in this year's midterm voting, if turnout is anything like the previous midterm in 2022; and as of October 12, a record $3.8 billion had been spent on political advertisements that have been aired so far. Top spending is in battleground US Senate races in Texas, Ohio and Michigan, according to AdImpact, which tracks the activities. [USN:L6N45Y0SX TEXT:"Elon Musk alone"] has spent about $366 million to support Republicans, according to campaign finance records. Still, midterms generally attract fewer voters than the higher-profile presidential races. More than 155 million votes were cast in the 2024 presidential election, for example. CONTROL OF CONGRESS AT STAKE Plenty is at stake in this midterm election as [USN:L6N45K0S4 TEXT:"Democrats try to win majority control"] of the US Congress. Currently, Republicans hold a 218-214 majority in the House, where there are two vacancies and one independent who caucuses with Republicans. Democrats must win a net gain of four seats to win control. Democrats also are fighting to win the Senate, where Republicans hold a 53-47 majority. They must net four additional seats to get control. [USN:L6N45U0XV TEXT:"Ten races,"] including those in Maine, Ohio, North Carolina, Iowa and Georgia, could decide the outcome. CAN MIDTERMS AFFECT THE PRESIDENCY? Midterm elections generally are dangerous territory for the political party that holds the White House and/or Congress. For 2026 that means that President Donald Trump and his Republicans controlling the US Senate and House of Representatives are in perilous political positions. The midterms can be an opportunity for voters to, in effect, [USN:L1N45V0SB TEXT:"grade the president's performance,"] and possibly trigger White House course corrections if they receive low marks. Midterm election results also can give aspiring presidential candidates hints on how to tailor their messages to voters in the next presidential campaign, which in this case will be in 2028. WHAT ARE POLLS SHOWING? Approval of [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"Trump's performance"] is at an all-time low of 32%, according to a September Reuters/Ipsos poll. [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"Domestic issues"] like rising consumer prices are likely to have an impact on the outcome of many races and could [USN:L1N45Z0VZ TEXT:"erode support for Republicans."] At the same time, there is evidence that [USN:L4N45T027 TEXT:"Democrats are more enthusiastic"] about voting this year than Republicans. If early voting trends continue it could point to a Democratic win in November. There are also signs that [USN:L6N44B0W4 TEXT:"Latino voters"] who veered to Trump in 2024 might be returning to Democrats because of frustration over the economy and some of Trump's immigration enforcement tactics. However, a landslide for the Democrats is [USN:L1N45N0R3 TEXT:"far from assured"]. Republicans could benefit from continued skepticism towards Democrats, a Republican spending advantage on campaigns, and fears from moderate voters over some primary wins by left-wingers. RECENT MIDTERM HISTORY Recent history tells the story of the shockwaves a midterm election can produce. In the 2010 midterms, during the Democratic presidency of Barack Obama, Republicans scored major victories, winning 63 additional House seats amid an underperforming US economy and weak support for Obama's landmark healthcare reform legislation. Democrats lost their majority. In the Senate, they held onto control despite losing six seats. The Republican wave was [USN:520101108 TEXT:"a "shellacking,""] Obama lamented at the time. He subsequently faced Republican demands for significant reductions to non-defense spending. Democrats [USN:KCN1NC0KY TEXT:"returned the favor"] in 2018, with Trump in the White House. They gained a net total of 40 House seats, but lost a net two Senate seats. This year's elections also have races for governors in 39 of the 50 states and voting in nearly every state for seats in their state-level legislative bodies. Currently, Republicans control 55% of state legislative seats across the country, while Democrats hold 43.8%, according to Ballotpedia. WHO WILL BE SPEAKER? If Democrats manage to win the House, the next speaker — second in line for the presidency after the vice president — is likely to be Democratic Representative Hakeem Jeffries of New York. He is currently the House Democratic leader. Jeffries, who would become the first Black American to hold the powerful office, would be in a position to direct House committees to [USN:L6N45E0PR TEXT:"launch investigations"] into a range of controversial activities by Trump and his associates. Jeffries repeatedly has said Democrats would look into what he has called "unprecedented levels of corruption" during the Trump administration. Jeffries also would steer Democrats' legislative priorities through the House. He has said Democrats would focus on making healthcare, groceries, housing, energy and other costs more affordable. A Republican win, on the other hand, would ensure that the speaker's gavel remains in that party's hands, either with current speaker Mike Johnson or whichever Republican prevails if he is challenged for the job. Republican priorities are likely to be focused on additional tax cuts, huge increases in defense spending, and deeper social safety net reductions, building on Trump's 2025 [USN:L1N3T10IT TEXT:""One Big Beautiful Bill.""] MARQUEE RACES [USN:L6N45U0XS TEXT:"Among the most-watched House races"] are Republican Representative Mike Lawler's bid for reelection to a New York district that Democratic candidate Kamala Harris won in her 2024 presidential campaign and an open seat in a Nebraska swing district where farmers and truckers face sharply higher fuel prices as a result of the US war against Iran. Also high on Democrats' list of House seats they hope to take from Republicans are two in Pennsylvania and one in New Jersey. Hovering over all of this are questions over whether Trump will try to meddle in the elections, which are administered by the 50 individual states. Since 2020, he has repeatedly insisted there is widespread cheating in US elections, despite a lack of evidence. State election officials and Democrats in Congress have been preparing for possible legal challenges to any moves by his administration to try to intervene.

item.title: European telecom groups mull bid for mobile satellite spectrum
item.description: Deutsche Telekom , Orange , Telefonica and Vodafone have agreed to explore a joint bid for the future allocation of spectrum for mobile satellite services in Europe, the network operators said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deutsche Telekom (DTEGn.DE) , Orange (ORAN.PA) , Telefonica (TEF.MC) and Vodafone (VOD.L) have agreed to explore a joint bid for the future allocation of spectrum for mobile satellite services in Europe, the network operators said on Monday. The aim is to meet customer demand for universal coverage in underserved areas, strengthen the resilience of public networks and protect critical communications. The four companies plan to establish key ground infrastructure as well as important coordination and control functions in Europe, they said. They will not invest directly in a satellite constellation, which will be provided by a satellite partner still to be selected. The letter of intent to explore a potential joint bid for MSS spectrum does not replace existing satellite partnerships.

item.title: Chinese oilfield service company Anton starts marketing Iraqi oil
item.description: China's Anton Oilfield Services Group said it has marketed its first Iraqi crude oil cargo under a new supply contract with state oil marketer SOMO, in a rare arrangement that helps Baghdad secure funds to pay for service providers.
item.dc:creator: Chen Aizhu
item.content:encoded: China's Anton Oilfield Services Group (3337.HK) said it has marketed its first Iraqi crude oil cargo under a new supply contract with state oil marketer SOMO, in a rare arrangement that helps Baghdad secure funds to pay for service providers. The Hong Kong-listed firm is one of a handful of Chinese independent oil companies ramping up operations in Iraq, Reuters has reported. Iraq is scrambling to boost oil sales disrupted by the Iran war now in its eighth month. In recent months, its oil exports have [USN:L1N45T01H TEXT:"rebounded as deeper discounts"] attracted traders and refiners. Anton said in a statement released on LinkedIn on Saturday that the deal aims to "support BOC's (Basrah Oil Company's) crude oil sales and cash flow, establish channels connecting engineering and services, crude oil sales and financial settlement, facilitate payment recovery for Anton and partners." Under the deal signed last month with SOMO, Anton will market an unspecified amount of Iraqi oil, mainly from the Majnoon oilfield operated by BOC, Iraq's state-run oil and gas producer, said an industry official with direct knowledge of the matter. The official declined to be named due to company policy. Anton lifted 1 million barrels of Basrah Heavy crude in late September and sold the cargo to a trading house, the industry official said. The Chinese firm said the marketing deal also paved the way for it to lift and market oil from Iraq's Dhufriya oilfield in the future. Anton was awarded a license to develop the Dhufriya oilfield in eastern Iraq in 2024, becoming a [USN:L4N3TR0SM TEXT:"project operator"] in the OPEC nation for the first time. The field is currently at an exploration stage, said the same official.

item.title: 中国首相、タジキスタンとの安全保障協力深化呼びかけ
item.description: [北京 １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 １９日 ロイター] - 中国の李強首相は１９日、中国政府が「過激主義」および「分離主義」と見なすものに対抗するため、タジキスタンとの安全保障・情報協力の深化を呼びかけ、同国が中国国民を保護するために「強力な措置」を講じることを期待すると述べた。

中国はかねてより、中央アジアでの暴力が、イスラム教徒が多数を占めるウイグル族が住む最西端の新疆ウイグル自治区に波及することを懸念してきた。中国は、新疆で過去に相次いだ一連の攻撃の背後にはウイグル過激派がいたと主張している。

中国国営の新華社通信によると、李首相はタジキスタンのラフモン大統領に対し、両国は法執行と安全保障における協力を深化させ、情報交換と共有を強化すべきだと伝えた。

また李氏は、中国とタジキスタンはテロリズム、分離主義、過激主義の「三つの悪の勢力」と共同で戦い、地域の平和と安定を守っていくべきだと語った。

人権団体は、中国がウイグル人を厳しく弾圧し、彼らの宗教的、文化的、言語的権利を制限していると指摘しているが、中国は、いかなる人権侵害も発生していないと否定している。

タジキスタンと山岳地帯で国境を接する中国は、同国への主要な投資国だ。

昨年末、タジキスタンで中国人５人が殺害される事件が発生したが、当局は、この攻撃が隣国アフガニスタンから仕掛けられたものだと発表した。

item.title: Seis migrantes, entre ellos un bebé, mueren tras una colisión de embarcaciones frente a la costa griega
item.description: Seis migrantes, entre ellos un bebé, fallecieron después de que una lancha rápida que transportaba a personas procedentes de Turquía chocara con una embarcación de la guardia costera griega y volcara frente a la isla de Lesbos en la madrugada del lunes, informaron las autoridades griegas, mientras el Gobierno prometía "tolerancia cero" contra los traficantes de personas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Seis migrantes, entre ellos un bebé, fallecieron después de que una lancha rápida que transportaba a personas procedentes de Turquía chocara con una embarcación de la guardia costera griega y volcara frente a la isla de Lesbos en la madrugada del lunes, informaron las autoridades griegas, mientras el Gobierno prometía "tolerancia cero" contra los traficantes de personas. El accidente se produjo a unas 3,5 millas náuticas (6,5 kilómetros) al sur de Agrilia, en Lesbos. La guardia costera indicó que los equipos de rescate recuperaron los cadáveres de cuatro hombres, una mujer y un bebé, mientras que ocho personas sobrevivieron y fueron trasladadas al hospital. Las autoridades detuvieron a un ciudadano turco de 37 años que se encontraba entre los supervivientes y lo identificaron como el presunto traficante y conductor de la embarcación. El ministro de Transporte Marítimo de Grecia, Vassilis Kikilias, culpó a los traficantes de migrantes de las muertes y afirmó que las pruebas disponibles hasta el momento indicaban que la lancha rápida había embestido con la proa el costado izquierdo de una embarcación de la guardia costera, añadiendo que se estaban investigando las circunstancias exactas. "Nuestra postura es innegociable: tolerancia cero con los traficantes", escribió en una publicación en la red social X. Grecia ha sido durante mucho tiempo una de las puertas de entrada preferidas a Europa para migrantes y refugiados procedentes de Oriente Medio, África y Asia. En 2015-2016, se situó en primera línea de la crisis migratoria europea y casi un millón de personas llegaron a sus islas, principalmente procedentes de Turquía.

item.title: Gaza-Faute de fonds, le PAM réduit son aide à 500.000 Palestiniens
item.description: Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) des Nations Unies a déclaré lundi que le manque de financement l'obligeait à réduire considérablement son programme d'aide à Gaza, laissant ainsi environ 500.000 personnes sans aide alimentaire mensuelle sur un territoire où les deux tiers de la population restent en situation d'insécurité alimentaire aiguë.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) des Nations Unies a déclaré lundi que le manque de financement l'obligeait à réduire considérablement son programme d'aide à Gaza, laissant ainsi environ 500.000 personnes sans aide alimentaire mensuelle sur un territoire où les deux tiers de la population restent en situation d'insécurité alimentaire aiguë. Le PAM a annoncé réduire le nombre de bénéficiaires de son aide mensuelle à 1,1 million de personnes, contre 1,6 million auparavant. De plus, les rations alimentaires ont été réduites de moitié, l'aide financière a été diminuée pour 75.000 familles et le nombre de repas chauds quotidiens pour les personnes incapables de cuisiner est passé de 250.000 à 150.000, certaines familles vivant dans des zones difficiles d'accès ne recevant désormais un repas chaud que tous les deux jours. Le PAM a déclaré qu'environ 1,4 million de personnes, soit les deux tiers de la population de Gaza, sont confrontées à une insécurité alimentaire critique, voire pire, dont environ 200.000 personnes en situation d'urgence. Le cessez-le-feu à Gaza, négocié l'an dernier sous l'égide des États-Unis, prévoit la reconstruction progressive du territoire. Cependant, peu de progrès ont été réalisés en vue de la mise en œuvre d'un accord visant à mettre fin au conflit, accord qui inclut le désarmement du Hamas et le retrait des troupes israéliennes. "Un an après l'entrée en vigueur de cet accord de cessez-le-feu, la vie reste brutale. Il n'y a pas d'abris décents, pas de services de base, pas de sécurité", a déclaré à Reuters à Gaza Carl Skau, directeur exécutif par intérim du PAM. "Ces coupes budgétaires interviennent alors que nous nous apprêtons à affronter le quatrième hiver. Vous savez, j'ai vécu des hivers ici, absolument terribles", a-t-il ajouté. Le PAM a déclaré avoir besoin de toute urgence de 450 millions de dollars (402 millions d'euros) au cours des six prochains mois pour maintenir ses opérations essentielles à Gaza et en Cisjordanie occupée par Israël. "Nous disons au monde entier que ce n'est pas le moment de détourner le regard. C'est le moment de redoubler d'efforts pour maintenir ce soutien, protéger les progrès accomplis, mais aussi pour favoriser une reprise rapide" de l'aide, a ajouté Carl Skau.

item.title: La police israélienne arrête 10 personnes en lien avec les diplomates européens attaqués par des colons en Cisjordanie occupée
item.description: La police israélienne a annoncé lundi avoir arrêté dix suspects dans le cadre de son enquête sur les incidents violents survenus ce week-end en Cisjordanie occupée, notamment des agressions menées par des colons juifs à la fois contre des diplomates européens et une journaliste du Washington Post.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La police israélienne a annoncé lundi avoir arrêté dix suspects dans le cadre de son enquête sur les incidents violents survenus ce week-end en Cisjordanie occupée, notamment des agressions menées par des colons juifs à la fois contre des [USN:L8N46309E TEXT:"diplomates européens"] et une [USN:L6N4620KJ TEXT:"journaliste"] du Washington Post. La France a [USN:L8N46402E TEXT:"condamné"] dimanche l'agression "gravissime" par des colons juifs du maire d'Aulnoye-Aymeries survenue la veille dans le village palestinien de Taybeh. La Belgique et la Pologne, dont des diplomates ont également été attaqués, se sont joints à Paris pour exhorter Israël d'agir. Et dès samedi, les Etats-Unis, proches alliés de Tel Aviv, ont demandé à Israël d'en faire [USN:L6N464002 TEXT:"davantage"] pour empêcher les attaques commises par les colons en Cisjordanie occupée. La police israélienne a précisé que les 10 personnes avaient été arrêtées lors d'une opération menée avant l'aube, ajoutant qu'elles étaient soupçonnées d'implication dans des actes de violence, d'avoir enfreint un arrêté interdisant l'accès à une zone militaire et d'avoir procédé à des constructions illégales. Les suspects, dont la police n'a pas révélé l'identité, ont été placés en garde à vue pour être interrogés. La radio de l'armée israélienne a noté qu'il s'agissait de citoyens israéliens. Les poursuites judiciaires à l'encontre de colons israéliens sont rares. Une vidéo diffusée par la police semble montrer qu'au moins un des suspects, dont on ne voit pas le visage, porte les franges rituelles appelées "tsitsits", généralement portées par les hommes juifs pratiquants. La vidéo montre également deux frondes découvertes dans l'une des propriétés. Vendredi, lorsque des dizaines de colons israéliens vêtus de noir et le visage masqué ont incendié des oliviers et lancé des pierres sur des Palestiniens dans le village d'Abou Falah, blessant au passage la journaliste du Washington Post, certains étaient armés de frondes. La police, les forces militaires et le Shin Bet, les services de sécurité intérieure, ont pris part à l'opération. Faisant référence à la Cisjordanie par son nom biblique, la Judée et la Samarie, le commissaire de police israélien Daniel Levy a déclaré que la loi s'appliquait à tous, "quelle que soit leur identité ou leur appartenance". "La police israélienne s'engage à faire respecter la loi de manière professionnelle, équitable et impartiale, sur la base de preuves et conformément à la loi", a-t-il déclaré dans un communiqué annonçant les arrestations. La violence des colons israéliens contre les Palestiniens en Cisjordanie occupée a connu une forte recrudescence ces derniers mois, avec au moins 170 attaques recensées depuis le 27 septembre, date correspondant approximativement au début de la récolte annuelle des olives, selon Yesh Din, une organisation israélienne de surveillance des colonies. Les colons sont galvanisés par le gouvernement de droite dure du Premier ministre Benjamin Netanyahu, qui a supervisé une expansion rapide des colonies et des avant-postes de moindre envergure à travers la Cisjordanie. Benjamin Netanyahu, dont la coalition est à ce stade donnée perdante par les sondages lors des élections législatives prévues le 27 octobre, a critiqué les violences des colons, mais n'a pris que peu de mesures pour réprimer ces incidents.

item.title: Putin respalda una remodelación menor del Gobierno ruso
item.description: El presidente de Rusia, Vladimir Putin, respaldó el lunes una remodelación del Gobierno aparentemente de escaso alcance propuesta por el primer ministro, Mijaíl Mishustin.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Rusia, Vladimir Putin, respaldó el lunes una remodelación del Gobierno aparentemente de escaso alcance propuesta por el primer ministro, Mijaíl Mishustin. La remodelación se produce tras las elecciones parlamentarias de septiembre, que renovaron la composición de la Duma Estatal, la cámara baja del Parlamento, y en un momento en que Rusia busca nuevas fuentes de crecimiento en medio de un déficit presupuestario creciente, impuestos más altos y tasas de interés relativamente elevadas. En uno de los cambios más destacados, Antón Siluánov pasará a ser vice primer ministro y seguirá al frente del Ministerio de Finanzas, cartera que ocupa desde 2011. Entre los demás cambios, el ministro de Transporte, Andréi Nikitin, fue propuesto para el cargo de vice primer ministro encargado, entre otras áreas, del desarrollo del sector del transporte. Dmitri Yádrov, director de la Agencia Federal de Transporte Aéreo de Rusia (Rosaviatsiya), fue propuesto para suceder a Nikitin como ministro de Transporte. Todos los cambios están sujetos a la aprobación parlamentaria.

item.title: A FONDO La prisa de España por resolver la situación en Ceuta desata alertas sobre derechos humanos
item.description: Cuando Fatna, en avanzado estado de embarazo, y su hijo discapacitado llegaron al enclave español de Ceuta, en el norte de África, durante un caótico cruce masivo de la frontera el 30 de julio, esperaba ser una de las primeras en recibir ayuda de las autoridades.
item.dc:creator: Corina Pons, Victoria Waldersee
item.content:encoded: Cuando Fatna, en avanzado estado de embarazo, y su hijo discapacitado llegaron al enclave español de Ceuta, en el norte de África, durante un caótico cruce masivo de la frontera el 30 de julio, esperaba ser una de las primeras en recibir ayuda de las autoridades. Casi tres meses después, con su hija recién nacida aquejada de problemas renales, Fatna, de 21 años, y su familia necesitan llegar urgentemente a la España peninsular para recibir tratamiento hospitalario especializado. Sin embargo, para viajar mientras se tramita su solicitud de asilo necesita un permiso que el Gobierno socialista español —por lo general partidario de la inmigración— se ha mostrado reacio a conceder a ninguno de los miles de migrantes que permanecen en Ceuta. Algunos siguen dispersos por las calles o escondidos en las onduladas colinas de la diminuta ciudad portuaria de 20 kilómetros cuadrados, situada en la frontera nororiental de Marruecos. El Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez, que se enfrenta a unas elecciones anticipadas el 29 de noviembre, se encuentra bajo la presión de la UE y de una población cada vez más frustrada para resolver la crisis. Está trabajando en procedimientos acelerados para las solicitudes de asilo con la intención de enviar a la mayoría de las personas de vuelta a sus países de origen, principalmente a Marruecos, al considerar que son migrantes económicos y no verdaderos solicitantes de asilo. Las ONG temen que esto suponga un riesgo de violación de los derechos de los migrantes. Sánchez, uno de los pocos dirigentes de izquierdas que quedan en Europa, dijo esta semana que España estaba gestionando la avalancha de casos "de forma responsable, con espíritu de solidaridad y respetando los derechos humanos de los migrantes". Sin embargo, más de 20 entrevistas realizadas por Reuters a migrantes, abogados, ONG y fuerzas de seguridad revelaron que muchos de los que permanecen en el país tienen motivos claros para solicitar asilo o protección humanitaria: desde menores no acompañados hasta marroquíes LGBTQ+ que temen ser encarcelados si son deportados, pasando por familias como la de Fatna, clasificadas como vulnerables según la legislación de la UE. La semana pasada, ocho organizaciones humanitarias, entre ellas Oxfam y Amnistía Internacional, presentaron una denuncia ante el Defensor del Pueblo español, a la que ha tenido acceso Reuters, en la que alegaban "graves violaciones de derechos" en el pequeño enclave de Ceuta. Entre ellas figuraban la devolución forzosa de migrantes procedentes de países en conflicto y la denegación de intérpretes y asistencia jurídica. Los portavoces del Gobierno central español, del Ministerio del Interior, del Ministerio de Política Territorial y del Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios de Reuters sobre las acusaciones de malos tratos. "Existen personas que realmente estarán en un peligro enorme si se las retorna a Marruecos", dice Wendell Soares, coordinador del centro católico de acogida de migrantes San Antonio, que ha acogido a la familia de Fatna y a decenas más de personas vulnerables, superando con creces su capacidad habitual de siete plazas. "Hay que analizar caso por caso porque no existe homogeneidad. Cuando se utiliza la palabra 'inmigrante', se crea una imagen colectiva como si todos fueran iguales. Cada persona tiene una historia, una motivación, un objetivo y hay que ver caso a caso". DEPORTADOS SIN EXPLICACIÓN Los partidos españoles de derecha y extrema derecha ya habían criticado al Gobierno de Sánchez por haber regularizado a casi un millón de migrantes en situación irregular a principios de este año. Han calificado la llegada masiva de julio como una invasión deliberada por parte de Marruecos —una acusación que Rabat niega— y han exigido que se devuelva a todos los migrantes. Con todo, a pesar de los planes para un nuevo procedimiento a escala de la UE que permita deportaciones aceleradas en futuras situaciones de emergencia, la normativa actual exige que se evalúe a los migrantes caso por caso. Aunque la mayoría procede de Marruecos, el Gobierno estimó en agosto que más de 1.000 de los migrantes que quedaban procedían de países subsaharianos, cuyos nacionales obtienen asilo en más del 90% de los casos en España, según estadísticas gubernamentales. El nuevo pacto de la UE exige que los casos se tramiten en zonas fronterizas para permitir deportaciones más rápidas. Sin embargo, no obliga a los solicitantes a permanecer en el lugar de llegada, lo que permite su traslado a otras zonas fronterizas de España, lo que aliviaría la presión sobre Ceuta, una población de 84.000 habitantes que constituye la única frontera terrestre de Europa con África junto con Melilla, otro enclave español. Si se quiere evaluar adecuadamente la situación de los migrantes vulnerables, estos traslados son la "única opción", dijo Juan Miguel Morales, director general de la ONG Sur Acoge. Aunque 262 menores han sido trasladados a la península desde la travesía de julio, la estrategia del Gobierno para los adultos restantes ha consistido en convencer al mayor número posible de que regresen por voluntad propia. El Gobierno ha declarado esta semana que 12.000 personas han optado por volver desde mediados de agosto. "No hay en ningún caso ninguna devolución encubierta", dijo el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, quien describió los retornos como voluntarios y añadió que se habían recibido hasta 1.200 solicitudes de asilo, de las cuales 700 ya se habían resuelto. Sin embargo, al menos nueve ONG han afirmado, en comunicados públicos o en entrevistas con Reuters, que los migrantes a los que prestan apoyo fueron coaccionados para regresar. La Asociación Elín señaló que migrantes de Sudán y Chad fueron citados por la policía los días 24 y 25 de septiembre y deportados sin previo aviso, según la denuncia presentada ante el Defensor del Pueblo. En mensajes de texto a los que ha tenido acceso Reuters, el migrante marroquí Azhaar Chaouni contó a voluntarios de la ONG alemana Mission Lifeline que él y otros migrantes corrieron la misma suerte, después de ser recogidos en autobuses por la policía en sus campamentos improvisados en la playa y de que les dijeran que los llevaban a centros de acogida. "Nos deportaron sin dar ninguna explicación", escribió Chaouni, indicando que se encontraba en Marruecos. La designación de Marruecos como "país de origen seguro" según la normativa de la UE no priva a sus ciudadanos del derecho a solicitar asilo, señaló Andrea de Petris, experto en inmigración del centro de estudios CEPN, con sede en Bruselas. "Se debe garantizar a cada persona una evaluación específica de sus circunstancias personales", añadió De Petris, quien estima que el procedimiento sería, inevitablemente, "largo y costoso". Las historias de otras personas que han desaparecido han infundido miedo en Rayane, un marroquí gay de 19 años que espera noticias sobre su solicitud de asilo en el centro de acogida de San Antonio. Rechazado por su familia y ante la imposibilidad de vivir en libertad en Marruecos, donde las relaciones sexuales entre personas del mismo sexo son perseguidas por la ley, está desesperado por llegar al continente europeo. "Ni siquiera puedo imaginarme volviendo a Marruecos. Me suicidaría antes incluso de cruzar la frontera", dijo. PACTO AL DESCUBIERTO Trabajadores de primera línea y ONG sobre el terreno afirman que la situación en Ceuta ha demostrado que el plazo de 12 semanas establecido en el pacto migratorio de la UE para tramitar las solicitudes de asilo es poco realista, y siete de ellos señalan que esperan que el proceso se prolongue durante meses. La falta de recursos, desde personal hasta computadoras que funcionen, hizo que, a fecha de 14 de octubre, solo se registraran unos 100 casos de migrantes al día, según el representante del sindicato policial Raúl Piera. El sindicato estima que aún hay entre 7.000 y 8.000 migrantes más dispersos por la ciudad, durmiendo a la intemperie o hacinados en instalaciones proporcionadas por organizaciones humanitarias y grupos de la sociedad civil que cubren el vacío dejado por los desbordados servicios sociales de Ceuta. "Teniendo en cuenta la carga de trabajo pendiente, esto se prolongará hasta bien entrado el próximo verano", dijo Piera. El Gobierno español no ha querido comentar las estimaciones sobre el número de migrantes no registrados, y el ministro de Política Territorial, Ángel Víctor Torres, dijo a los periodistas el 14 de octubre que era imposible saber cuántos se encontraban ocultos. Los médicos del único hospital de Ceuta están tratando a migrantes que padecen sarna, tuberculosis e infecciones gastrointestinales provocadas por los largos periodos que pasan a la intemperie, según explicó Enrique Robiralta, presidente del sindicato de médicos. Al menos siete mujeres han dado a luz. Fatna y su esposo Mohamed están desesperados por quedarse en España, preocupados por la bebé y convencidos de que su hijo discapacitado de 3 años morirá en Marruecos. "Estamos haciendo todo por nuestro hijo", dijo Mohamed.

item.title: フィリピンが中国大使を召喚、「武力行使」ほのめかす発言巡り
item.description: [マニラ １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[マニラ １９日 ロイター] - フィリピン外務省は１９日、中国の井泉駐フィリピン大使を呼び出し、同大使の発言が武力行使の脅威をほのめかしているとして、「深刻な懸念と強い抗議」を表明した。

井大使は先週、メディアに対し、フィリピンとの対立において中国は「容易に勝利できる」と述べた一方で、「われわれは平和を愛している」ため、中国は武力を行使しないと語った。これは、フィリピンの国防相が中国を「地域のトラブルメーカー」と表現したことに対する質問への回答だった。

フィリピン外務省の声明によると、ラザロ外相は井氏に対し、その発言は「挑発的かつ容認できない」ものであり、両国間の緊張した雰囲気を悪化させたと伝えた。

ラザロ氏は、敏感な問題は、対話と関与の余地を残す確立された外交ルートや二国間メカニズムを通じて対処されるべきだと述べた。

南シナ海の島や岩礁を巡り対立してきた中国と、米国の同盟国フィリピンはたびたび激しい応酬を繰り広げている。

中国外務省は１９日、フィリピンの一部の議員による井氏の召喚や追放要求について問われると、一部の個人による中国関連問題の「悪意ある誇張」に断固として反対すると表明した。

同省報道官は定例記者会見で「フィリピン側は、一部の政治家によるこうした無責任な言動を抑制するための具体的な措置を講じるべきだ」と述べた。

また、二国間関係の改善は両国にとって利益になると述べた。

item.title: Rain delays start of second day’s play between South Africa and Australia
item.description: Rain delayed the start of play on the second day of the second test between South Africa and Australia in Gqeberha on Monday. South Africa were on 20 runs for two wickets after only 60 minutes of play was possible at St George’s Park on the opening day on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rain delayed the start of play on the second day of the second test between South Africa and Australia in Gqeberha on Monday. South Africa were on 20 runs for two wickets after only 60 minutes of play was possible at St George’s Park on the opening day on Sunday. Debutant Marques Ackerman (5) and home skipper Temba Bavuma (4) were due to resume, but no start time was scheduled. An umpires' inspection was set for 11:15 a.m. (0915 GMT). The weather is set to clear later on Monday, and no more rain is forecast for the rest of the test. Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls on Sunday to give Australia a strong start after they had won the toss and put the home side into bat. Australia lead the three-match series after a 214-run victory in the first test at Kingsmead in Durban last week.

item.title: Mozambique courts South African investment for new gas project
item.description: Mozambique's state-owned oil company ENH is in talks with potential investors, including South Africa's Sasol and pipeline company ROMPCO, for a new natural gas project as the country aims to become a regional "power hub", the chief executive of ENH said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mozambique's state-owned oil company ENH is in talks with potential investors, including South Africa's Sasol (SOLJ.J) and pipeline company ROMPCO, for a new natural gas project as the country aims to become a regional "power hub", the chief executive of ENH said. Mozambique, the primary supplier of gas to South Africa from Sasol’s onshore Pande and Temane fields that are expected to be depleted within a few years, has massive resources in its offshore Rovuma Basin and could help meet South Africa’s future gas demands. The new project, centred on the coastal towns of Beira and Inhassoro, is expected to cost about $250 million and would involve the development of floating storage and regasification units (FSRU) at Inhassoro and the Port of Beira. A new 140 kilometre pipeline would connect the facilities to the larger ROMPCO pipeline, the main gas artery running from Mozambique to South Africa's Secunda industrial complex. ENH is part of a group of state-owned companies handed an exclusive [USN:L8N3X009A TEXT:"30-year concession"] last year to build and operate natural gas facilities in the Southern African country where oil companies TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) , ExxonMobil (XOM.N) and Eni (ENI.MI) are developing [USN:L4N44E17T TEXT:"large LNG"] plants. "We want our infrastructure by 2030 or 2031, in step with Mozambique LNG, Rovuma LNG and [USN:L8N46118B TEXT:"Coral North"]," Rudencio Morais, the CEO and chairman of ENH, told Reuters in an interview. Gas from these developments is mostly destined for international markets, although new petroleum laws in place since June require at least 25% of gas and oil production, now explicitly including LNG, to be allocated to the domestic market. "Mozambique is going to become what we call the power hub," Morais said as the country looked to export gas into a region plagued by power shortages. Sasol said it would be premature to speculate on the nature or scale of any potential investments as it sought alternative gas supplies, while ROMPCO did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Albert Heijn online deliveries to stay offline until at least Thursday after cyber incident
item.description: Ahold Delhaize's Albert Heijn, the largest supermarket chain in the Netherlands, will not resume online deliveries before Thursday at the earliest, according to a message in its app on Monday, extending to at least 11 days an outage caused by what the company has called a "cybersecurity incident".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ahold Delhaize's (AD.AS) Albert Heijn, the largest supermarket chain in the Netherlands, will not resume online deliveries before Thursday at the earliest, according to a message in its app on Monday, extending to at least 11 days an outage caused by what the company has called a "[USN:L8N45Z1DC TEXT:"cybersecurity incident"]". Websites and delivery services of the company's Dutch and US chains remained offline on Monday, a week after the incident prompted it to shut down some of its own IT systems Collectively, the US brands, which include Stop & Shop, Giant Food, Hannaford and Food Lion, form one of the largest food retailers in the United States Deliveries at the Belgian Delhaize chain were resumed over the weekend Ahold said on Friday it was working on a "controlled relaunch" of several systems The company has so far declined to share details of the incident, saying investigations are ongoing It has said there was no evidence that any customer data had been stolen Physical stores of several chains have remained open, but have struggled with supplies as distribution channels were also affected

item.title: Zetwerk's $518 million India IPO fully subscribed on final day of bidding
item.description: Peak XV Partners and Accel India-backed Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses' $518 million initial public offering was fully subscribed on last day for bids on Monday, exchange data showed, led by demand from qualified institutional buyers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Peak XV Partners and Accel India-backed Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses' $518 million initial public offering was fully subscribed on last day for bids on Monday, exchange data showed, led by demand from qualified institutional buyers. Here are some details: Industrial and consumer goods manufacturer Zetwerk counts wind turbine maker Siemens Gamesa, Acer India, NTPC Renewable Energy, and the Indian Air Force among its major clients The IPO received bids for 220.4 million shares, against 185.1 million shares on offer, as of 2:00 p.m. IST Qualified institutional investors bid for 1.63 times, non-institutional and retail portions were subscribed 0.79 times and 0.51 times The company is seeking a valuation of up to 255.83 billion rupees ($2.69 billion) at the upper end of the IPO price band of 143-151 rupees per share Proceeds will be used to prepay and repay borrowings as well as fund inorganic growth opportunities Last week, Zetwerk raised 22.51 billion rupees from anchor investors, including Capital Group, BlackRock and Goldman Sachs The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to 28.3 billion rupees and an offer for sale of 144.53 million shares by existing investors The offer for sale includes 51.4 million shares from co-founders Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan and Creovate Innovation Venture investors Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed and Accel India are also trimming their holdings The stock is expected to begin trading on October 23 ($1 = 94.9300 Indian rupees)

item.title: VW plans to freeze salaries until 2030, works council says
item.description: Volkswagen plans to freeze salaries for its 660,000 staff worldwide until 2030, the group's works council said on Monday, confirming an earlier report by Sueddeutsche Zeitung.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen plans to freeze salaries for its 660,000 staff worldwide until 2030, the group's works council said on Monday, confirming an earlier report by Sueddeutsche Zeitung. The Global Works Council said it had received internal information about the executive board's plans Volkswagen declined to comment on "speculation". A spokesperson added that a new round of talks later this week would be the forum for any proposals on labour costs The works council called the management's approach "absurd" and said it expected strong resistance to what is described as the plan's "rather unrealistic" implementation "At Volkswagen, pay development is decided at the negotiating table, not by decree from the executive boardroom," a spokesperson for Germany's trade union IG Metall said Relations between Volkswagen and its labour representatives have deteriorated in recent months, as CEO Oliver Blume pushes ahead with the most [USN:L8N44W0B8 TEXT:"radical restructuring"] in the German auto group's history The Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported the news earlier on Monday, citing internal documents The absence of pay rises could mean a loss of income of around 10% for those affected, due to inflation, the paper said The paper report said the new global management guidelines, effective from the fourth quarter, also include cuts to variable pay, special payments, benefits, and jobs.

item.title: Pedidos de recuperação judicial no agro caem 20,7% no 2ºtri, diz Serasa
item.description: O agronegócio do Brasil contabilizou 448 pedidos de recuperação judicial no segundo trimestre, 20,7% abaixo do registrado em igual período do ano anterior, marcando a primeira queda para um segundo trimestre desde 2022, segundo análise da Serasa Experian divulgada nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O agronegócio do Brasil contabilizou 448 pedidos de recuperação judicial no segundo trimestre, 20,7% abaixo do registrado em igual período do ano anterior, marcando a primeira queda para um segundo trimestre desde 2022, segundo análise da Serasa Experian divulgada nesta segunda-feira. O indicador, que reúne pedidos realizados por produtores rurais que atuam como pessoa física e jurídica, além de empresas relacionadas à cadeia produtiva, mostrou uma retração também na comparação com os primeiros três meses de 2026, quando as solicitações de RJ somaram 474 (-5,5%). A desaceleração observada, apesar de positiva diante do cenário atual de endividamento dos produtores rurais, deve ser interpretada com cautela, disse o head de agronegócio da Serasa Experian, Marcelo Pimenta. "A retração nesse segundo trimestre registrada em pelo menos dois dos três perfis analisados pode estar relacionada a um período de maior entrada de receitas para parte dos produtores, à sazonalidade das atividades agropecuárias e ao avanço de renegociações com credores", explicou Pimenta. "Por isso, é importante acompanhar se essa redução será sustentada nos próximos trimestres", acrescentou, lembrando que o ambiente segue desafiador, com custos elevados e crédito mais seletivo. O Mato Grosso, principal produtor de grãos, oleaginosas e gado do Brasil, seguiu na liderança do número de pedidos de RJ entre os Estados, totalizando 107 registros. Ele foi seguido por Goiás (84), São Paulo (72), Minas Gerais (54) e Paraná (42). No recorte por atividade, o cultivo de soja -- o principal do Brasil -- concentrou 70 solicitações de recuperação judicial, seguido pela criação de bovinos, com 28, segundo a Serasa. Os pedidos de RJ de produtores rurais que atuam como pessoa física caíram 10,5% frente ao segundo trimestre de 2025, para 197, enquanto as solicitações por parte de produtores pessoa jurídica recuaram 34,2%, a 160. Na análise por porte, os produtores classificados como "sem propriedades", que pode envolver arrendatários, concentraram 70 pedidos. Em seguida, aparecem os grandes proprietários, com 51 solicitações; os pequenos proprietários, com 39; e os médios proprietários, com 37.

item.title: IW-Studie: Viele Deutsche sind reicher als sie denken
item.description: Viele Deutsche ordnen sich der Mittelschicht zu, gehören aber oft schon zu den Besserverdienern. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt eine am Montag veröffentlichte Studie des arbeitgebernahen Instituts der deutschen Wirtschaft (IW) in Köln. Wer als Alleinlebender im Jahr 2024 über ein monatliches Nettoeinkommen von mehr als 6050 Euro verfügte, zählte bereits zu den einkommensreichsten vier Prozent der Bevölkerung. Zur Mittelschicht im engeren Sinne gehörte ein Single demnach mit einem Einkommen zwischen 1940 und 3630 Euro netto. Die Untersuchung zeigt, dass viele Menschen ihre eigene Position in der Einkommensverteilung falsch einschätzen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Viele Deutsche ordnen sich der Mittelschicht zu, gehören aber oft schon zu den Besserverdienern. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt eine am Montag veröffentlichte Studie des arbeitgebernahen Instituts der deutschen Wirtschaft (IW) in Köln. Wer als Alleinlebender im Jahr 2024 über ein monatliches Nettoeinkommen von mehr als 6050 Euro verfügte, zählte bereits zu den einkommensreichsten vier Prozent der Bevölkerung. Zur Mittelschicht im engeren Sinne gehörte ein Single demnach mit einem Einkommen zwischen 1940 und 3630 Euro netto. Die Untersuchung zeigt, dass viele Menschen ihre eigene Position in der Einkommensverteilung falsch einschätzen. Ein Grund für die verbreitete Fehleinschätzung ist den Autoren zufolge, dass sich die meisten Menschen vor allem mit Personen aus ihrem direkten Umfeld mit ähnlichem sozioökonomischem Hintergrund vergleichen. "Reich sind vor allem die anderen – dieser Eindruck ist nachvollziehbar, kann aber täuschen", sagte die IW-Ökonomin Judith Niehues. So hätten Personen mit Hochschulabschluss im Median über ein bedarfsgewichtetes Einkommen von 3140 Euro verfügt und damit bereits zum oberen Drittel der Gesamtverteilung gehört. Besonders viele Wohlhabende gibt es demnach unter Paaren ohne Kinder, bei denen beide Partner arbeiten. Knapp zwölf Prozent von ihnen erreichten die für diesen Haushaltstyp geltende Reichtumsschwelle von 9070 Euro netto im Monat. Das mittlere bedarfsgewichtete Haushaltsnettoeinkommen lag der Studie zufolge bei 2419 Euro im Monat. Dabei handelt es sich um einen statistischen Mittelwert, der alle Haushaltsgrößen vergleichbar macht und die Bevölkerung in eine reichere und eine ärmere Hälfte teilt. Die Studie basiert auf den neuesten verfügbaren Befragungsdaten zu Einkommen und Lebensbedingungen in der EU für das Jahr 2024. Das IW stellt zudem einen interaktiven Rechner zur Verfügung, mit dem die eigene Position in der Einkommensverteilung ermittelt werden kann. "Wer erwerbstätig ist und einen höheren Bildungsabschluss hat, hat in Deutschland gute Chancen auf ein vergleichsweise hohes Einkommen", so die Verteilungsexpertin Niehues.

item.title: 光部品・デバイスの湖北工業、26日付でプライム市場に変更
item.description:
Shinichi Uchida
［東京 １９日 ロイター］ - 光部品・デバイス事業を手掛ける湖北工業は１９日、東...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
光部品・デバイスの湖北工業、26日付でプライム市場に変更 17:31 配信

Shinichi Uchida

［東京　１９日　ロイター］ - 光部品・デバイス事業を手掛ける湖北工業は１９日、東証の承認を受け、上場市場区分が２６日付で東証スタンダード市場からプライム市場に変更されると発表した。自動車や産業機器などで使われるアルミ電解コンデンサ用リード端子や、海底ケーブル用光アイソレータで世界シェアトップとされている。

同社株の流通株式比率は６月末で３８．０８％で、プライム市場の上場維持基準（３５％以上）に近い水準にある。今後の状況次第では適合状況に影響を及ぼす可能性もあり、その場合は大株主による株式売り出し、新株発行などの資本政策を含め対応を適切に検討するという。
