item.title: Bomb threat forces Austrian Tel Aviv-Vienna flight to land in Bulgaria
item.description: A bomb threat forced an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna to divert to Sofia late on Sunday, though a search found nothing dangerous so the plane took off again and flew onwards, the airline and Bulgaria's BTA news agency said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A bomb threat forced an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna to divert to Sofia late on Sunday, though a search found nothing dangerous so the plane took off again and flew onwards, the airline and Bulgaria's BTA news agency said. BTA said the flight's crew reported receiving a bomb threat when the aircraft was approaching the Romanian border, and the Bulgarian Air Force scrambled MiG-29 fighter jets. Israeli newspaper Haaretz said the threat was "called in by an Austrian national who was not on board", without identifying its source. "We confirm that there was a threat against flight OS82 on October 18, 2026, from Tel Aviv to Vienna (TLV to VIE), which made it necessary for the flight to make an intermediate landing in Sofia (SOF)," the airline said in a statement on Monday. "During the search of the affected aircraft, the passengers, and the crew, no danger was identified," it said, adding that the flight continued from Sofia to Vienna with all passengers after reboarding. The plane was carrying 51 passengers and 6 crew, Austrian said. Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said it was an Airbus A320-200 series aircraft, which Austrian's website says has a capacity of up to 180 seats. Vienna Airport, the Austrian interior ministry and the Lufthansa Group (LHAG.DE) , which owns Austrian Airlines, did not respond to requests for comment. The Austrian and Bulgarian interior ministers were due to hold a previously scheduled press conference in Vienna later on Monday at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT). The incident took place less than three weeks after a co-pilot on an Israel-bound flydubai jet [USN:L6N46405H TEXT:"allegedly attacked"] the captain with an axe in an attempt to crash the plane. The United Arab Emirates' attorney general said last week an Omani flydubai co-pilot had intended to seize the September 30 Dubai-Tel Aviv flight and crash it into a terminal at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport in a suicide attack, before he was thwarted by the captain.

item.title: Oil slips from 5-month high as Trump's Russia sanctions waiver may bring more supplies
item.description: Oil prices slipped from a five-month high on Monday as investors took profits after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead to more Russian fuel exports.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: Oil prices slipped from a five-month high on Monday as investors took profits after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead to more Russian fuel exports. Brent crude futures fell $2.29, or 2.08%, to $107.57 a barrel by 0619 GMT after settling at its highest since May 19 on Friday. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $99.46 a barrel, down $1.95, or 1.92%, after closing at its highest since September 17 on Friday. Trump signed an [USN:L6N464042 TEXT:"executive order"] on Friday waiving key sanctions and tariffs under the law known as the Graham Act, which he signed last month at the urging of lawmakers who wanted to pressure Moscow over its war in Ukraine. However, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president will use up to 60 days to assess the impact of the sanctions and tariffs on the global economy. "Trump's move looks like another desperate attempt to keep oil prices in check ahead of the US midterm elections," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insight at Phillip Nova, adding that it does little to address the physical supply disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, where oil tanker attacks continue. KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer said while the US waiver on Russian sanctions could lead to higher Russian fuel exports, the mixed messaging has created uncertainty. "Until the details and duration are clearer, the market is unlikely to fully price in a sustained increase in supply," he added. The waiver comes after Trump struck a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin to export diesel to the United States and other countries — starting at about 2.3 million barrels this month before rising to about 7.6 million barrels monthly. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said these US actions will [USN:L6N46405N TEXT:"hurt Ukraine."] MIDDLE EAST CRUDE EXPORTS FALL SHARPLY Brent crude oil briefly touched $110 a barrel on Friday for the first time since May as tensions and security threats in the Middle East raised concerns over the safety of shipping and tighter global energy supplies. Intensified attacks on commercial vessels cut Gulf crude flows sharply to about 8.5 million barrels per day on a seven-day average last week from more than 20 million bpd the week before, analytics firm Kpler said in a note on Friday. At least 10 confirmed incidents involving commercial vessels were reported last week, it added. Potentially raising the stakes in the Middle East war, [USN:L1N46401H TEXT:"Egypt"] said it is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability against Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis. DBS expects oil prices to remain rangebound in the $100 to $110 a barrel range going into the US midterms as Iran and its proxies would ensure oil prices and domestic fuel prices remain the key irritant for US voters. "The US president is trying various moves to suppress prices ahead of the midterms without any direct concession to Iran," its head of energy research Suvro Sarkar said. "However, all the levers he has pulled – including waivers on Russia sanctions – are short-term fixes and will have barely any structural impact on the supply situation."

item.title: 債券売りでインフレ鈍化へ＝ラガルドＥＣＢ総裁
item.description:
Francesco Canepa
[バンコク １７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１７日、債...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
債券売りでインフレ鈍化へ＝ラガルドＥＣＢ総裁 7:09 配信

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁。10月14日、バンコクで撮影。REUTERS/Athit Perawongmeth

Francesco Canepa

[バンコク １７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１７日、債券売りによってユーロ圏の借り入れコストが上昇し、経済成長が抑制され、最終的にインフレも鈍化するとの見方を示した。

ここ数週間、債務やインフレへの懸念に加え、人工知能（ＡＩ）投資に伴う資金調達競争の激化を背景に、世界的に債券利回りが急上昇している。多額の債務を抱えるフランスは、特に大きな打撃を受けている。

ラガルド氏は、こうした状況により、消費者がイラン戦争に伴う燃料価格の上昇を吸収することは、ＥＣＢが９月に予測した以上に難しくなるとの見方を示した。

タイの首都バンコクに集まった各国の中央銀行総裁や財務相を前に、ラガルド氏は「経済成長は底堅さを保っているが、前回の会合以降、長期金利が著しく上昇するなど資金調達環境は引き締まっている」と指摘。「これにより成長が鈍化し、価格転嫁は９月の予測以上に抑制されるだろう」と語った。

ＥＣＢは過去４カ月間で２回利上げを実施し、１２月にも追加利上げが見込まれている。実施すれば政策金利は２．７５％となり、ＥＣＢが景気抑制的と見なす水準に達する。

ＥＣＢ理事会メンバーのナーゲル独連銀総裁も、今後の追加引き締めを示唆した。ただ、政策は入手するデータに基づき、会合ごとに判断するとした。

バンコクで開かれたＤＺ銀行のイベントで「われわれはインフレと闘っている。仕事はまだ終わっていないと考えている」と述べ、「さらなる対応が必要になる可能性がある」と語った。

同じ場で発言したＥＣＢ理事会メンバーのレーン・フィンランド中銀総裁は、エネルギー価格の上昇が他の物価や賃金に波及する「二次的影響」をＥＣＢは注視すると述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＥＣＢ「予防的」追加利上げへ、米イラン紛争長期化で アングル：ＥＣＢ、金利据え置きへ　原油価格が再び焦点 アングル：ＡＩの経済金融への影響、ＥＣＢフォーラムで希望と懸念が交錯 アングル：金融市場はＥＣＢのタカ派化見込む、イラン戦による油価高騰で コラム：求むＥＣＢ総裁、危機に強い革新者 最終更新: 10/19(月) 7:09 ロイター

item.title: 豪チャレンジャー、第一ライフグループが未保有株取得へ予備的提案
item.description: [１９日 ロイター] - オーストラリアの保険会社チャレンジャーは１９日、第一ライフグループの豪子会社から、未保有の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
豪チャレンジャー、第一ライフグループが未保有株取得へ予備的提案 7:04 配信

第一ライフグループのロゴ。4月6日、東京で撮影。 REUTERS/Issei Kato

[１９日 ロイター] - オーストラリアの保険会社チャレンジャーは１９日、第一ライフグループの豪子会社から、未保有のチャレンジャー株を取得する予備的提案を受けたと発表した。提案は同社の企業価値を７９億４０００万豪ドル（５５億３０００万ドル）と評価しているという。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、ＴＡＬダイイチライフ・オーストラリア（ＴＤＡ）はチャレンジャー株２０．３６％を保有している。

第一ライフ側は１株当たり１１．８０豪ドルでの取得を提示した。チャレンジャー株の前週末１６日終値に１９．８％のプレミアムを乗せた水準となる。

提案には資産査定（デューデリジェンス）が満足のいく形で完了することなど、複数の条件が付いている。

チャレンジャーは声明で「当社取締役会は暫定的な提案を検討している」とした。

第一ライフは報道を受け、ＴＤＡがチャレンジャーに対し法的拘束力のない提案を提出したことを確認している、としたうえで、「現時点で法的拘束力のある取引を進めることに関して決定した事実はない」とのコメントを公表した。

Oct 19 : A unit of Japan's Daiichi Life has made an indicative proposal to buy more than 79 per cent of shares in Australian investment manager Challenger it does not already own, Challenger said on Monday. Shares of the Australian firm jumped over 15 per cent to A$11.33 by 2305 GMT, hitting their highest level since October 23, 2018. Under the proposal, the Japanese insurer is offering A$11.80 apiece, valuing Challenger at A$7.94 billion ($5.53 billion). The offer represents a premium of 19.8 per cent over the stock's closing price on Friday. The unit, TAL Daiichi Life Australia Pty, holds 20.36 per cent of the Australian investment manager, according to LSEG. Daiichi Life, through its unit, had initially acquired a 15.1 per cent minority stake in Challenger from MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings in April 2025.

"The Board of Challenger is considering the indicative offer," the Australian firm added. In a separate statement, Daiichi Life confirmed that TAL Daiichi Life Australia has submitted a non-binding proposal to the board of directors of Challenger, adding that no decision has been made by the company on proceeding with the binding transaction. Separately, Challenger reported a 5 per cent rise in its assets under management to $31.9 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, citing strong sales momentum across both domestic and offshore annuities. item.title: Antofagasta’s Centinela strike ends after deal with unions
item.description: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contra
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contract, ending a strike of more than a week, the unions and the company said on Sunday. More than 700 members of the Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions began the strike on October 7 after contract talks broke down. They had sought equal benefits for workers regardless of which union they belonged to. The parties returned to the negotiating table on Tuesday in an effort to resolve the dispute. “The Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions announce the successful conclusion of our collective bargaining process, after 94.49% of participating workers voted to approve the proposed collective agreement,” the unions said in a statement, which was followed by a company statement confirming the deal. Three workers had been on a hunger strike in an effort to pressure both sides into finding a solution to the deadlocked talks. Antofagasta said on Wednesday it had managed to maintain production at normal levels, avoiding any negative impact from the strike at the mine, which produced 240,400 metric tons of copper in 2025. The strike at Centinela, along with the ultimately unrealized risk of a supervisors’ strike at BHP’s Escondida mine, had been supporting global copper prices amid concerns about the industry’s ability to increase supply sufficiently to meet expected future demand. (Reporting by Fabian Cambero; Editing by William Mallard)

US officials visit Palestinian village after settler attacks on diplomats

US Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labor Riley Barnes visits the Christian Palestinian village of Taybeh near Ramallah, a day after Israeli militant settlers attacked a French mayor and European diplomats during olive harvest, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct 18, 2026. FAST

TAYBEH, West Bank: US diplomats visited a Christian Palestinian village in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday (Oct 18) following attacks by militant Israeli settlers on European diplomats and an American photojournalist in the previous two days. Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labor, Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See, and a number of other diplomats visited the Latin Convent church and were expected to meet with members of the Christian community in Taybeh. Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor and Palestinian civilians, had been attacked near Taybeh on Saturday by masked Israeli settlers. The previous day, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village.

The diplomats' visit coincided with US President Donald Trump endorsing his ally, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for Israel's parliamentary election on Oct 27. Meanwhile, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee attended a settler conference in the West Bank on Sunday. Huckabee, an evangelical Christian and longtime supporter of Israel, earlier wrote on X calling for "those who attacked" the Washington Post photojournalist, a US citizen, to be jailed.

Related:

Israel denounces 'grotesque absurdity' of Macron UN remarks on West Bank

Israel's Netanyahu orders West Bank settler outposts to be removed, sources say

US ambassador visits Palestinian town amid rise in West Bank settler violence

NETANYAHU CIRCUMSPECT ON SETTLER VIOLENCE Trump has expressed his opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank, but his administration has put little pressure on Netanyahu's right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military both blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack on the diplomats, Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect. He has said the diplomats entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination" with the Israeli military, and that the facts of the attack on Levine are "unclear". France urged Israeli authorities to arrest Saturday's attackers and to end criminal violence in the West Bank, but by Sunday there was no announcement from Israeli authorities of any arrests in either of the two latest incidents.

Israeli settlers attack a journalist in Abu Falah, West Bank Oct 16, 2026, in this screengrab from a video. (Photo: Andrey X/via REUTERS)

The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinian s. Settler attacks on the Palestinian s are surging, with at least 170 since Sep 27, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli human rights group. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. Yet prosecutions of Israeli settlers are rare. On Sunday, Reuters saw a group of at least 10 settlers, masked and dressed in black, hurling rocks at Palestinian s and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian West Bank town of Salfit, prompting the farmers to flee. Israeli border police were in the area and shot tear gas towards the hills.

Source: Reuters/fs

FAST

Oct 18 : AI lab Anthropic, the developer of Claude, said on Sunday it will commit 5 per cent of its shares to a new public benefit fund so it has increased flexibility and scale to make donations for the "public good." The proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2 per cent of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50 per cent increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. The move comes at a time when Anthropic is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a public benefit corporation, a legal structure that requires management to consider certain broader interests as well as turning a profit for investors. The company, which has positioned itself as a safety-first AI lab, has said AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" and devoted roughly 80 pages of the 261-page main body of its prospectus to laying out risk factors.

Anthropic said in its blog post its Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI’s impact on the labor market.  Elon Musk, who runs Anthropic rival xAI, on X said he recommended "giving the shares directly to the public." Anthropic cited the potential impact of AI on workers as one area of focus for the new fund, building on a previously announced $200 million commitment to study and address labor-market disruption. Global companies have cut thousands of jobs after investing heavily in AI, with many, primarily tech firms, pointing to higher efficiencies from the technology's rapid adoption. IMF research shows that some 40 per cent of jobs will be either augmented, downgraded or eliminated by AI, with the number as high as 60 per cent in advanced economies, Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said last week. NOT FOR POLITICAL GIVING The AI giant said none of the equity held by its fund would be used for lobbying or political giving in the United States or abroad. US policymakers are weighing greater oversight of artificial intelligence and AI companies are stepping up efforts to shape how the technology is regulated. Combined with its co-founders' pledge to donate 80 per cent of their equity and an employee donation matching program, roughly 20 per cent of Anthropic's shares will be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares added later. Anthropic said it would say more in the coming months on the fund's governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake. It also plans to publish a public-benefit report detailing progress toward its mission.

Source: Reuters

item.description: The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210km east of Edmonton in Alberta.

Strong winds fuelled grass fire at Canadian military base that killed four

The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210km east of Edmonton in Alberta.

A sign for Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire that caused deaths and injuries, in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada on Oct 18, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Jennifer Gauthier)

CALGARY: Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smouldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday (Oct 18). Officials said 39 people were in hospitals as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which Prime Minister Mark Carney described as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on home soil. Winds up to 96km per hour fed the blaze which began around 4pm MDT on Saturday. But they were below 50kmh leading up to the fire, Major General Wade Rutland told reporters at a news conference. He described the sudden high winds and resulting spread of the fire as an "uncommon, rapid" event in which the flames advanced 1km in 30 to 60 seconds.

"I’ve certainly never seen anything like it," said Rutland, commander of 1st Canadian Division, which is based in Edmonton, about 210km west of the military site. Officials identified the dead as Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell, Private Aidan Goulding and Private Hayden Lykkemark. "The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honour the victims. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said many of the injured will require "weeks and months" of specialised, intensive medical care. When the fire began, Rutland said, 85 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, were in "high intensity" combat training using live munitions at the base, which is located in a prairie setting. The soldiers were preparing for deployment to Latvia, where Canadian forces currently have their largest international military operation. Rutland said the incident remains under investigation and declined to speculate on what caused the grass fire. Officials do not believe the region's extensive oil and gas infrastructure had anything to do with the incident, he said. He also ruled out "outside interference." CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country.

People attend a church service, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire caused deaths and injuries at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada, Oct 18, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jennifer Gauthier)

Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable", Carney said. Twenty-two ground ambulances and eight air ambulances responded to the scene, Smith said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer. Military search and rescue technicians also parachuted into the site, Rutland said. Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright. The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base. The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

Source: Reuters/fs/ec

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 18) endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election. Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minster" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilising regional economies. "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure - But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today."

Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote. It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era. Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to Trump on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!" Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries, including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras.

item.title: Arsenal edge Forest with late goal, Man United held by Leeds
item.description: Champions Arsenal needed a late goal from Noni Madueke, their only shot on target, to scrape a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest and remain three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Champions Arsenal needed a late goal from Noni Madueke, their only shot on target, to scrape a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday and remain three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City. Brighton & Hove Albion's Diego Gomez struck a sensational goal from inside his own half in a 5-0 rout of Crystal Palace on Sunday to leave his side third in the table with 16 points, five behind leaders Manchester City. Manchester United and bitter rivals Leeds United shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw at Elland Road at the end of a turbulent week for the Red Devils in which defender Lisandro Martinez had publicly challenged the club's hierarchy. Leeds are seventh in the table and Manchester United, who have just one win from seven games, are 13th. Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 for their first league victory of the season to climb to 15th place. Sunderland remained in the drop zone in 19th place. At the City Ground, a frustrated Arsenal finally sealed victory in the 80th minute. Ibrahim Sangare hesitated when he could have cleared the ball, leaving Forest manager Oliver Glasner visibly fuming, and second-half substitute Madueke then danced past Daniel Munoz before hammering a shot that deflected off Jair Cunha and wrong-footed Matz Sels. "We're really happy, we did it all together. We showed grit, determination, and maybe we showed a champion spirit here for that, really pleased," Madueke told Sky Sports. Murillo almost salvaged a point for Forest in injury time when he beat three players before unleashing a shot that sailed agonisingly wide. The defeat left Forest, who have yet to win or even score at the City Ground this season, in the drop zone in 18th place with five points. At the Amex, Brighton got on the scoresheet in the fourth minute through a Jaydee Canvot own goal, before Gomez struck a goal of the season contender three minutes later, robbing Adam Wharton of the ball near the halfway line before taking a touch and firing the ball over keeper Walter Benitez and into the net. "When I got the ball I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead," Gomez told Sky Sports. "When I scored I didn't know where to run or what to do. I was very happy with the goal." Yasin Ayari padded Brighton's lead three minutes later, before Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood completed the rout after the break. Kostoulas scored just after halftime when Ayari's shot deflected into the Greece international's path, and Hinshelwood struck in the 84th when Luka Vuskovic's header was scooped off the line by Benitez and he fired home the rebound. MBEUMO GRABS OPENING GOAL Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the 35th minute after missing a couple of chances. Mbeumo held off James Justin before tapping in a Youri Tielemans cross from six yards out. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised in the 51st minute, chesting down the ball from a corner before poking home. "We are slightly disappointed it is just a point," Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky. "Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. "We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester United." Manchester defender Martinez retained his place in Michael Carrick's starting lineup despite criticising United's hierarchy following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, questioning the club’s summer investment and singling out director of football Jason Wilcox before later apologising. Bournemouth punished a shaky Sunderland start to take the lead after just six minutes, when Lewis Cook lofted a long ball forward that Evanilson ran on to and squared for Marcus Tavernier to head home from close range. Evanilson scored himself in the 48th minute when the Brazilian rounded goalkeeper Robin Roefs before slotting home left-footed.

Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday (Oct 18), as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensify their attacks on the world's largest oil exporter. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support. A parliamentary vote had been expected on authorizing the request for military support on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said. HOUTHIS RAMP UP ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the state oil giant Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce.

"Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites," the Egyptian presidency said in a statement. It followed a meeting of Egypt's National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief. Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed Salman, who visited Sisi on Sep 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited. Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of President Mohamed Morsi in 2013. Egypt had previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 to support the government against the Houthis, but played a limited combat role.

item.title: In France's Limoges, the fire-ravaged town hall rekindles memories of Notre Dame
item.description: The ornate 19th century neo-Renaissance building which survived two world wars was torched by a masked mob.
item.dc:creator: Clotaire Achi
item.content:encoded: Residents in Limoges recoiled in horror on Sunday at the city's fire-ravaged town hall, an ornate 19th century neo-Renaissance building which survived two world wars but was torched by a masked mob during the [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"worst unrest"] to convulse France in years. Stunned onlookers had watched helplessly the previous evening as the blaze tore through the roof, felling the building's clock tower in scenes that revived haunting memories of the collapse of Notre Dame cathedral's spire in a 2019 fire. "It broke my heart. I saw Notre Dame all over again, except this time it was our town," said Francoise Faurie who witnessed the fire consume Limoges' town hall. Faurie's family had been due to celebrate her grand-daughter's baptism in the town hall in a month's time. "What kind of country are we living in? What are we leaving our children?" she said. "There's no reason to touch that building. You can have demands, you have the right to protest, but not the right to violence." EXTENSIVE DAMAGE The local prefect, Maurice Barate, said the roof had caved in onto lower floors, sparing only the west wing, and that large parts of the exterior had been destroyed. The destruction of the building, a listed monument that opened in 1883 and was inspired by Paris' city hall, was a "heritage catastrophe", he said. Its central clock tower and belfry towered 43 metres (141 feet) over the square below. "It's inadmissible to have burned down the town hall!" one local resident, Gilbert, said. "Those who did this need to be punished. They need to pay out of their own pocket, it's not for the state to pay." The town's shaken mayor, Guillaume Guerin, described how the local police force had quickly been overwhelmed by several hundred-strong mob who he said smashed windows and used a battering ram to break down the main door. "The logistics, the organisation, the premeditation behind yesterday’s attack on the town hall is something I find unbearable," he told reporters. Guerin said there had been insufficient police numbers to protect the building since officers from the national force had been deployed to the street protest. "I had no single national police officer to protect the town hall," the centre-right mayor continued. "This country is doing badly, this country is doing very badly, and it’s a small provincial mayor telling you so." Crowds gathered under blue skies as specialists surveyed the damage. Edith Lorcen, a retired nurse, expressed her shock at the malice of those behind the attack. "I'm disgusted. I'm hurting," Lorcen said. "But it does nothing to add hate on top of hate."

Oct 18 : Microsoft has pulled out of a data center deal with British cloud provider Nscale, Britain's Telegraph newspaper reported on Sunday. The US tech giant, one of Nscale's two largest customers, recently terminated its agreement for the data center in Loughton, Essex, according to the report. The newspaper did not specify why Microsoft withdrew from the project. Microsoft declined a Reuters request for comment. The Telegraph report said Nscale had faced repeated delays with the project. National power grid officials, it reported, had told Nscale they did not expect a power supply for the data center until the 2030s.

item.title: Macron urges calm as France counts cost of worst unrest in years
item.description: The French president appealed for calm a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with thousands arrested and shops looted or damaged after protests over high prices and declining public services.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide, Clotaire Achi, Abdul Saboor
item.content:encoded: President Emmanuel Macron appealed for calm on Sunday, a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with thousands arrested and shops looted or damaged after protests over high prices and declining public services. Fresh clashes broke out in Paris and Marseille, where riot police intervened to prevent attempts to ransack businesses. Nationwide demonstrations had erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops pillaged and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. "Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: What was going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?" Macron said in a televised address to the nation. "Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame." Saturday's unrest laid bare the deep anger at Macron, who leaves office in 2027 after a decade in power that has increasingly become defined by social discontent, a weak economy and ballooning debt. Macron said those protesting peacefully had legitimate grievances and their actions should not be confused with those seeking to wreak havoc. He stopped short of declaring a state of emergency, as demanded by some right-wing politicians, but said the government would act to allow prefects to ban protests if necessary to protect public buildings and local businesses. PARIS PROTESTS 'LIKE A WAR ZONE' The government has blamed the violence on what it said were ultra-left groups, as well as criminals it said had instigated the looting. One protester died on Saturday after suffering a cardiac arrest during [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"demonstrations"] in Paris. Police made 2,400 arrests across France, while nearly 1,000 officers were injured, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Police again clashed with protesters and fired tear gas at Place de la Republique on Sunday afternoon, and protesters had set fire to piles of bicycles. A Reuters witness said there appeared to be several hundred protesters in the area. A massive clean-up operation took place in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and from Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect. "It's like a war zone here!" exclaimed Dutch entrepreneur Tije De Boer, who was visiting Paris with his children and said the unrest forced him to evacuate his hotel at Place de la Republique. More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities on Saturday, marking the convergence of a month-long [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"student movement"] with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services. SEVERAL HUNDRED SHOPS DAMAGED While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully across France on Saturday, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets, and attacked police vehicles and officers. Far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, frontrunner going into next year's presidential campaign, also called for calm, saying France must not become accustomed to images of the country being battered, abused and ransacked. "Violence is not an opinion. Destruction is not a form of expression. And chaos cannot serve as a project for France," she said in a video address. Hard-left France Unbowed presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said Macron needed to answer the demands of protesting high-school students. In [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], famed for its porcelain, the collapse of the town hall's clock tower in a fiery blaze revived memories of the 2019 fire that devastated Paris' Notre Dame cathedral. Mayor Guillaume Guerin said not enough officers from the national police had been deployed to his city. "There was a clear, premeditated intention to burn down the town hall, and the people inside feared for their lives," Guerin told Reuters on Sunday. He threatened to resign if the city did not receive the funds needed to repair the town hall. Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support on Sunday for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement. French retailer Carrefour's (CARR.PA) CEO Alexandre Bompard told French broadcaster BFMTV that 50 of the company's shops had been damaged, including 20 that were looted, with losses from the damage running into the tens of millions of euros.

item.title: ソフトバンクＧ、米警備大手アライド買収検討＝関係筋
item.description:
Milana Vinn
[１６日 ロイター] - ソフトバンクグループが米警備サービス大手アライド・ユニバーサルの...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ソフトバンクＧ、米警備大手アライド買収検討＝関係筋 10/17 15:08 配信

ソフトバンクグループのロゴ。９月東京で撮影。REUTERS/Manami Yamada

Milana Vinn

[１６日 ロイター] - ソフトバンクグループが米警備サービス大手アライド・ユニバーサルの買収を検討している。関係者が１６日明らかにした。買収案では、アライドの評価額が約１８０億ドルになる可能性がある。

アライドは企業や各種施設、大規模イベントに警備員を派遣する事業を手がける。データセンター分野でも事業を拡大しており、施設の開発と運営の両面を支援している。

ソフトバンクはアライドの買収が実現すれば、特定の警備業務で人員の一部をいずれロボットに置き換えることを目指す。ただ人型ロボットの警備業務への導入には長い時間がかかるとみられる。

買収検討は初期段階にあり、買収額を含め、最終決定には至っていないという。

item.title: 海外勢の米国債保有、8月は9.33兆ドルに増加 英加がけん引
item.description: [ニューヨーク １６日 ロイター] - 米財務省が１６日発表した８月の対米証券投資統計によると、海外勢の米国債保有残...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
海外勢の米国債保有、8月は9.33兆ドルに増加　英加がけん引 10/17 6:34 配信

米ドル紙幣。３月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[ニューヨーク １６日 ロイター] - 米財務省が１６日発表した８月の対米証券投資統計によると、海外勢の米国債保有残高は９兆３３１０億ドルと、前月の９兆２４８０億ドルから増加した。２カ月連続の減少から増加に転じた。英国とカナダの保有が増加をけん引した。

前年同月比では１％弱の増加にとどまった。

日本の保有高は８月に１兆０６８０億ドルと、７月の１兆１０３０億ドルから３．２％減少し、４カ月連続の減少となった。ただ、日本は海外勢としては依然として米国債の最大保有国だ。保有額は２０２１年１１月に１兆３２５０億ドルでピークを付けた。

海外勢の保有額で２位の英国は、８月の保有高が前月の９９８３億ドルから１．１％増の１兆００９０億ドルとなり、初めて１兆ドルの大台を突破した。

中国の保有高は５９０７億ドルと、７月の６１８０億ドルから２．４％減少し、２００８年８月以来の低水準となった。減少は３カ月連続となった。中国は海外勢の保有額で依然として３位だが、８月の保有額は前年比で約１６％減少した。

米国債は１０８９億ドルの買い越しとなった。７月は３６億ドルの売り越しだった。

米社債は４１６億ドルの買い越しとなり、前月の２６９億ドルから増加した。

対米証券投資は１９９８億ドルの買い越し。前月の８７４億ドルから増加した。

item.title: ＮＹ市場サマリー（16日）10年債利回り週間で大幅低下、ドル軟調 株反落
item.description: ＜為替＞ ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対して下落した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測の後退に加え、ＡＩ（...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ市場サマリー（16日）10年債利回り週間で大幅低下、ドル軟調　株反落 10/17 6:10 配信

＜為替＞　ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対して下落した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測の後退に加え、ＡＩ（人工知能）関連銘柄主導の株安への懸念が引き続き重しになっている。    米国では今週発表された９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）と９月の卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）をが予想を上回って伸びたことなどで、一時的に利上げ観測が再燃。ただその後、ＦＲＢ当局者の発言で追加利上げを急がない姿勢が示されたことで、ドル相場に対する支援材料も薄れていた。    今週はこのほか、ＡＩ関連銘柄が大幅に下落。ＡＩ関連銘柄やサプライチェーン全体に資金を投じてきた投資家の間でデータセンター運営企業が債務返済に必要な利益を十分なタイミングで確保できるのか疑念が広がっていることが背景にあり、影響はドル相場にも波及している。    ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長はバンコクで開かれた国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で行った講演で、米経済の力強さについて楽観的な見方を示すとともに、エネルギーショックが続きインフレ抑制に向けた金融引き締めが行われる中でも、世界経済が持ちこたえていることに驚きを表明。ＦＲＢの金融政策については「予断を持たない」と述べるにとどめ、追加利上げの可能性について手掛かりは示さなかった。    ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、今月の会合で金利据え置きが決定される確率は８３％。１カ月前の４９％から大きく上昇した。    終盤の取引で、ドル／円は０．０８％安の１ドル＝１５８．１１円。日銀の植田和男総裁は１６日、基調的な物価上昇率について、２％に「かなり近づいている」と指摘する一方で、２％目標に到達したかの判断は２９日からの金融政策決定会合で「政策委員の間でしっかり議論して結論を出したい」と述べるにとどめた。    ユーロ／ドルは０．０８％高の１．１２２７ドル。    主要６通貨に対するドル指数は０．１７％安の１０１．８７。

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞　指標となる１０年債利回りが週間ベースで１年超ぶりの低下幅となる見通しとなった。足元の経済指標を見極める動きが見られる中、市場では米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の次回利上げは１２月まで見送られるとの見方が強まっている。    午後の取引で１０年債利回りは横ばいの５．０８７％。一時、５．１３３４％まで上昇していた。ただ、週間ベースでは、２０２５年８月１日終了週以来の低下幅となる見通しとなった。    この日発表の経済指標では、９月の米輸入物価指数は前年比で８．１％上昇と、２０２２年７月以来の大幅な伸びとなった。中東紛争が続く中、インフレ圧力が高まっていることを改めて示唆した。    ＦＲＢのウォーシュ議長は１６日、バンコクで開かれた国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で、金利決定については「予断を持たない」と表明。今月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で利上げするか、据え置くかについては手掛かりを示さなかった。    市場ではＦＲＢが１０月２７─２８日のＦＯＭＣで金利を据え置くとの見方が一段と強まり、ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場が織り込む据え置きの確率は約８３％、１２月の利上げ確率は約８８％となった。    ２年債利回りは３．２ｂｐ低下の４．７１９％。一時、４．７８３％まで上昇していた。    ３０年債利回りは０．５ｂｐ上昇の５．４３３％。一時、５．４６４％を付けていた。     ２年債と１０年債の利回り格差は３６．６ｂｐ。    物価連動国債（ＴＩＰＳ）と通常の国債の利回り差で期待インフレを示すブレーク・イーブン・インフレ率（ＢＥＩ）は、１０年物が２．３４７％となった。

米金融・債券市場：[US/BJ]

＜株式＞　反落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービス大手コアウィーブやブロードコムなどＡＩ関連のハイテク株が再び売られたほか、原油価格の急伸も重しとなった。    エヌビディアが出資するコアウィーブは１２％下落。直近５営業日の下げ幅は約２５％となった。同社の社債は今週、大きく売り込まれ、利回りは１５％を超えた。    ブロードコムは４．５％下落。フィラデルフィア半導体指数は３．８％安となり、２００８年以来となる８営業日続落となった。    ナスダック総合は週前半からの下落幅を拡大した。多額の債務を抱えるＡＩインフラ企業が、借り入れコストの上昇が見込まれる中、債務返済に見合うだけの利益を期日までに計上できないのではないかとの懸念が圧迫した。     Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の主要１１業種のうち６つが上昇。エネルギーが２．４７％上昇でトップ、公益事業が１．４％上昇と続いた。    その他の個別銘柄では、電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラは３．１％下落。同社は、ロケットのような推進装置（スラスター）を搭載した新デザインのスポーツカー「ロードスター」を公開し、２０２８年に生産を開始すると発表した。    動画配信大手ネットフリックスは２．８％下落。同社は、最高コンテンツ責任者として元ディズニー幹部のピーター・ライス氏を起用すると発表した。    来週からは第３・四半期決算シーズンが本格化し、テスラ、メタ・プラットフォームズ、プロクター・アンド・ギャンブルなどが決算を控える。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、アナリストは四半期利益がＡＩ関連の大型株にけん引され、平均で３０％超急増すると予想している。    Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種では値下がり銘柄数と値上がり銘柄数がほぼ拮抗した。    米取引所の合算出来高は１８６億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７７億株。

米国株式市場：[.NJP]

＜金先物＞　米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測が強まる中、金相場は小動きとなり、週間では下落の見通しとなった。中心限月１２月物の清算値は０．３％高の１オンス＝４１８１．１０ドル。金現物は、米東部時間午後２時７分（日本時間１７日午前３時７分）時点で０．１％安の１オンス＝４１６５．１２ドル。週間では０．７％下落した。

米卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）と消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が予想を上回る伸びを示したことで、ＦＲＢによる年内追加利上げの可能性が意識されている。ＦＲＢのウォーシュ議長は米経済の強さに楽観的な見方を示したものの、利上げ方針については明言しなかった。市場では今月の利上げは見送られるとの見方が大勢だが、１２月の利上げ確率は９０％とされている。

ＮＹ貴金属：[GOL/XJ]

＜米原油先物＞　大幅高となり、北海ブレントが一時１バレル＝１１０ドルと５月以来の高値を付けた。中東情勢の緊迫化で供給が一段と逼迫するとの懸念が広がったほか、ロシアからの世界市場向けディーゼル燃料の供給能力に不透明感が強まったことが背景。    清算値は、北海ブレント先物が３．９４ドル（３．７％）高の１０９．８６ドルで、５月１９日以来の高値。米ＷＴＩ先物は３．４４ドル（３．５％）高の１０１．４１ドルで、９月１７日以来の高値となった。    今週に入ってブレントは４．９％、ＷＴＩは１０．４％、それぞれ上昇した。

ＮＹＭＥＸエネルギー：[CR/USJ]

item.title: Novartis ends mid-stage Fabhalta trial targeting serious kidney condition
item.description: Swiss drugmaker Novartis has terminated a mid-stage study testing its drug Fabhalta in patients with a serious kidney condition, citing "strategic considerations", according to a federal clinical trials registry.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swiss drugmaker Novartis (NOVN.S) has terminated a mid-stage study testing its drug Fabhalta in patients with a serious kidney condition, citing "strategic considerations", according to a federal clinical trials registry. The trial was evaluating whether the oral medication was safe and effective for treating lupus nephritis when added to standard medical care Lupus nephritis is a severe inflammation of the kidneys caused by the autoimmune disease lupus The government database, last updated on October 15, shows Novartis decided to conclude the study after completing the first part "The decision was based on strategic considerations and was not driven by any interim efficacy or safety findings," the company said, adding that other studies with the drug will continue as planned Investigators for the terminated trial have been notified and are engaging with participants regarding next steps, Novartis added Endpoints News reported the development on Friday The US FDA first approved Fabhalta in 2023 for a rare blood disorder called PNH. It has since been approved for two kidney diseases, IgA nephropathy and C3 glomerulopathy

item.title: The races that will decide control of the US Senate
item.description: Democrats need to pick up at least four seats in November's midterm elections to win control of the 100-seat US Senate, where Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority. That was seen as unlikely at the beginning of the year, but President Donald Trump's unpopularity and voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices have made many races competitive even in states that he won handily in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Mccaskill, Andy Sullivan
item.content:encoded: Democrats need to pick up at least four seats in November's midterm elections to win control of the 100-seat US Senate, where Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority. That was seen as unlikely at the beginning of the year, but President Donald Trump 's unpopularity and voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices have made many races competitive even in states that he won handily in 2024. Here are the races that will determine control of the Senate: MAINE Democrats' top opportunity to pick up a seat is in Maine , the lone state where a Republican incumbent is up for reelection in a state Trump lost in 2024. Republican Senator Susan Collins has distanced herself from Trump and declined to appear in the state with Vice President JD Vance. During a debate earlier this month, Collins — who voted to convict Trump after he was impeached following the January 6 insurrection — acknowledged that she isn't the president's favorite senator and said he won't be coming to Maine. Democrats say she only votes against Trump in the Senate when it doesn't matter — such as when she voted against a sweeping tax-cut package last year after backing it in a procedural vote. Democrats hope voters will hold her accountable for helping confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the US Supreme Court, which led to the overturning of a federal right to abortion. Democrats, however, have their own drama. The party's original nominee, [USN:L1N42G0S1 TEXT:"progressive oysterman Graham Platner"], was [USN:L6N43A0RY TEXT:"pressured into withdrawing"] following sexual assault allegations, forcing the state party to scramble for a new candidate. Platner has denied the allegations. Former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, another progressive, [USN:L6N43P103 TEXT:"emerged as Platner's replacement"]. Jackson has nearly caught up to Collins on the fundraising front. He has raised $20.4 million so far, with $4 million unspent as of September 30, while Collins has raised $24 million, with $5.4 million still in the bank. Outside groups are spending heavily as well. AdImpact, a monitoring service, predicts they will spend a total of $199 million on this election — equal to $171 for every adult in the state. Republican groups are outspending Democrats here, but most opinion polls show Jackson holding a narrow lead. OHIO Democrat Sherrod Brown is seeking to return to the Senate after losing his seat in 2024, and [USN:L1N45V0SB TEXT:"working-class frustration"] with the Iran war and rising prices may be giving him a tailwind. This time, Brown faces US Senator Jon Husted, who was appointed to the Senate to replace Vance when he left office for the White House. The Ohio race has become one of the most expensive Senate contests in the nation. AdImpact estimates Republican groups will spend $246 million on ads, while Democrats will spend $177 million. Brown has $16 million available for the final stretch, while Husted has $8.8 million. Recent polls show Brown leading by between 1 and 8 percentage points. ALASKA Trump traveled to Alaska last week to shore up incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is facing a stiff challenge from Democrat Mary Peltola, a former US Representative. Alaska allows voters to rank their top picks rather than choosing a single candidate. Voters will have four choices, including Sullivan, Peltola and another Dan Sullivan, a candidate Republicans have called a decoy in what they believe is a Democratic effort to confuse voters. Peltola has outraised Sullivan, but the Republican enters the final stretch of the campaign with $5.1 million in the bank, compared to $3.1 million for Peltola. Outside Republican groups have spent $33 million, while Democratic groups have spent $27 million. Trump won Alaska by 13 points in 2024, but recent polls show Peltola leading or tied with Sullivan. TEXAS No Democrat has won statewide in Texas since 1994. James Talarico, a state representative, could break the streak. Talarico faces a historically weak Republican nominee in Attorney General Ken Paxton, but Texas is still Texas — a big, conservative-leaning state that has dashed Democratic hopes repeatedly in recent years. Trump won Texas by nearly 14 points in 2024. Yet outside Republican groups have already spent a staggering $240 million to hold the seat after runoff voters [USN:L6N41V0YO TEXT:"nominated the scandal-plagued Paxton"] over incumbent Republican US Senator John Cornyn. [USN:O8N40E01T TEXT:"Trump endorsed Paxton"] even though Cornyn was widely believed to have an easier path to victory. Leaked audio has exposed daylight between Trump and Paxton, who privately told donors that the president's midterm convention hurt his campaign. Democratic groups have spent $50 million on this race, far less than Republicans. But Talarico's campaign has outraised Paxton's by $49 million and reported $16 million more in its campaign coffers as of September 30. Opinion polls show the race ranging from a tie to a 6-point Talarico lead. IOWA Trump's unpopularity, tariffs and the Iran war have put Republicans on defense in Iowa , where Trump won by 13 points in 2024. Republican US Senator Joni Ernst's decision not to seek reelection has made this an open-seat contest between Republican Representative Ashley Hinson and Democratic state Representative Josh Turek, a two-time Paralympic gold medalist. Hinson has called for an "immediate end" to the Iran war and said Iowans should not have to pay higher fuel or grocery prices as a result of it. However, she has repeatedly voted against resolutions in Congress calling for an end to the war. Hinson has outraised Turek and had $6.9 million available to spend as of September 30, nearly three times what Turek has in his war chest. Outside Republican groups have spent $61 million to Democrats' $55 million. Recent polls show the race effectively tied. MICHIGAN The [USN:L1N4420RK TEXT:"Democratic establishment didn't get its pick"] in Michigan . Progressive outsider Abdul El-Sayed narrowly defeated moderate US Representative Haley Stevens during the primary, putting him on a collision course with Republican Mike Rogers, a former US Representative, in what could be the tightest race for a Democratic-held Senate seat this year. Rogers has said Canada is not the United States' enemy, distancing himself from the president and his tariffs. Former Vice President Kamala Harris has campaigned with El-Sayed, and former President Barack Obama is set to rally with him later this month. The latest batch of polls shows El-Sayed leading by between 1 and 7 percentage points. Republicans have spent $104 million in Michigan's Senate race, nearly double Democrats' $55 million. NEW HAMPSHIRE Democrats are defending another open seat in New Hampshire , though this is a state Harris won by nearly 3 points in 2024. Democratic US Representative Chris Pappas is running against former US Senator John Sununu, who was ousted by Democrat Jeanne Shaheen in 2008. Shaheen is retiring. Sununu benefits from a famous last name. His brother Chris was governor until last year and his father — also named John — was a governor and White House chief of staff for President George H.W. Bush. Republicans have outspent Democrats in this race, $30 million to $15.5 million. Pappas has maintained a consistent polling lead of 5 to 8 points in recent surveys. GEORGIA Incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff appears to be holding his own against a challenge from Republican Representative Mike Collins in Georgia , a state Trump won by 2 percentage points in 2024. Recent polls show Ossoff holding a double-digit lead, and some outside Republican groups have pulled out of the race. Ossoff holds a clear financial advantage. He has raised $98 million as of September 30, with $26.3 million still unspent. Collins, by contrast, has raised $11 million and has $1.1 million available. NORTH CAROLINA Republicans appear to have conceded North Carolina , where outside spending groups have dropped their support significantly in recent weeks. Opinion polls show former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper holding a steady lead over former Republican National Committee Chair Michael Whatley, a Trump ally. It's a pickup opportunity for Democrats, as Republican Senator Thom Tillis is not seeking reelection. Cooper has raised $47.2 million, more than three times as much as his opponent, and has $12.5 million left to spend. Whatley has less than $1 million in the bank. Trump won North Carolina by 3 points in 2024. KANSAS The political environment has shifted in favor of Democrats so much that Kansas is now in play. Republicans have diverted resources from North Carolina to shore up US Senator Roger Marshall, who in recent weeks has condemned the activity of Immigration and Customs Enforcement in his state. Trump won Kansas by 16 points in 2024, but the state has twice elected Democratic Governor Laura Kelly. And Republican leaders have acknowledged the race is competitive and closer than they would like it to be. Marshall's opponent is Adam Hamilton, founding pastor of a Methodist megachurch. Marshall's campaign has outraised Hamilton's by $3 million and has nearly $1 million more unspent. In a reversal of the usual pattern, Democratic groups have outspent Republicans here, $16 million to $11 million. Recent polls show Hamilton leading by between 1 and 3 percentage points.

item.title: US House races to watch in the 2026 elections
item.description: Republicans in the US House of Representatives are defending a narrow majority in November's midterm elections. History suggests Democrats will gain seats - they would need to net four to win control of the chamber. But Republicans kickstarted a national redistricting battle that could make Democrats' path to a majority slightly more difficult.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Mccaskill
item.content:encoded: Republicans in the US House of Representatives are defending a narrow majority in November's midterm elections . History suggests Democrats will gain seats - they would need to net four to win control of the chamber. But Republicans kickstarted a national redistricting battle that could make Democrats' path to a majority slightly more difficult. Here are some races to watch: CAN LAWLER DEFY TRUMP'S GRAVITY? US Representative Mike Lawler of New York is one of just three Republicans who represent a congressional district Kamala Harris won in 2024. The others are an open seat in Nebraska and a Pennsylvania district US Representative Brian Fitzpatrick is favored to win. That makes Lawler the most vulnerable House Republican up for reelection. His opponent, Cait Conley, is a combat veteran and national security expert. Lawler has outraised Conley and Republican outside groups have likewise outspent Democrats in this district, $6.3 million to $5 million. Two polls conducted in late September show both Lawler and Conley with narrow leads in this toss-up race. REPUBLICAN REDISTRICTING MAY GO SOUTH IN TEXAS When Texas Republicans kicked off a national gerrymandering war against Democrats in the hopes of defying historical trends to hold their fragile majority in Washington, they sought to pick up five seats. Yet as Election Day nears, three of those seats are in play - [USN:L6N44B0W4 TEXT:"all in South Texas"]. Democratic US Representatives Vicente Gonzalez and Henry Cuellar are now running in districts President Donald Trump would have won by 10 percentage points in 2024. The third district, which was redrawn from a safe Democratic seat into one Trump also would have carried by 10 points, is an open race between Republican Carlos De La Cruz and Democrat Johnny Garcia. Gonzalez faces Republican Eric Flores, a former Texas Army National Guard infantry captain and former assistant US attorney. Republican groups have spent $8.8 million on this race, compared with $7.8 million by Democrats. DAVIS TRIES TO DEFY A NORTH CAROLINA GERRYMANDER Republicans redrew Democratic US Representative Don Davis' district, shifting it from a North Carolina district Trump won by 3 points to one he would have carried by double digits. Davis is seeking reelection anyway. Democrats have outspent Republicans in this district, $9.5 million to $7.5 million. A GOLDEN FLIP IN MAINE? The retirement of centrist Democratic US Representative Jared Golden in a district Trump won by 9 points in 2024 opened a key flip opportunity for Republicans. Former Maine Governor Paul LePage is running against progressive state auditor Matt Dunlap. LePage has outraised Dunlap and had nearly $1 million available to spend at the end of September. House Democrats' campaign arm added Dunlap to its "Red to Blue" program for top offensive opportunities in August. Polls last month showed Dunlap holding a slim lead over LePage. HIGH HOPES IN OHIO US Representative Max Miller of Ohio was reelected by 15 points in 2024, though an independent candidate got 13% of the vote. Trump won the district by a smaller margin than Miller, and domestic and child abuse allegations have made the congressman uniquely vulnerable. Miller has denied the allegations, but US Senator Bernie Moreno, a fellow Ohio Republican, has [USN:L6N43Z04U TEXT:"called on him to resign"] and end his reelection campaign. Moreno's daughter is Miller's ex-wife. The once safe seat is now seen as a toss-up. Brian Poindexter, the Democratic nominee, is an ironworker, a Brook Park city councilor and a member of Democrats' Red to Blue program. Democrats have poured $8 million into flipping the seat, compared to Republicans' $3.3 million. THIRD TIME'S A CHARM IN IOWA? US Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks of Iowa faces a familiar opponent in former state Representative Christina Bohannan, a Democrat who ran unsuccessfully against Miller-Meeks in 2022 and 2024. This time, however, could be different. Trump is deeply unpopular, and the combination of tariffs and the war in Iran has elevated cost-of-living concerns. Trump's policies have driven up the price of diesel and fertilizer as voters have said affordability is their top issue this cycle. Democrats have outspent Republicans here, $8.3 million to $6.8 million. SOUTH FLORIDA REPUBLICAN BREAKS WITH TRUMP ON IMMIGRATION "Mr. President, some of your immigration efforts have gone too far." [USN:L6N4590UZ TEXT:"That warning came last month"] from an incumbent Republican, US Representative Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida , who represents a district Trump won by nearly 15 points in 2024. Salazar is still favored to win reelection, but her high-profile break with the president on a signature issue is a sign Republicans could lose ground with the Latino voters who helped return Trump to the White House. Like Salazar, her opponent, Eliott Rodriguez, is a former TV news anchor. Democrats added Rodriguez to their Red to Blue program last week but haven't invested much money in his race, though they've outspent Republicans by about $200,000. WILL VOTERS SEND MGP BACK TO WASHINGTON? Centrist Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington authored a resolution condemning a fellow Democrat and helped Republicans advance their agenda by bucking her party on traditionally party-line procedural votes. That may help her in a district Trump narrowly won in 2024. Gluesenkamp Perez finished second in Washington's top-two primary, trailing state Senate Republican Leader John Braun. Republicans have outspent Democrats, $8.9 million to $3.5 million. DEMOCRATS RAISING THE BAR IN KENTUCKY? Democrats only hold one of Kentucky's six US House seats. But they see an opening in the 6th District, where incumbent Representative Andy Barr is the Republican nominee for US Senate. The Republican nominee is Ralph Alvarado, a former Kentucky state senator and ex-head of the Tennessee health department. His opponent is Democrat Zach Dembo, an ex-Navy JAG officer and former federal prosecutor. There's little daylight between the candidates in fundraising, and both parties have poured roughly the same amount of money into the race. Trump won the district by 15 points in 2024. MAY THE BEST DEM WIN California's top-two primary system occasionally pits two members of the same party against each other in a general election. This year, US Representatives Ken Calvert and Young Kim — both Republicans — are running for the same seat after Democrats redrew the state's congressional map. US Representative Doris Matsui, a Democrat, is similarly facing Sacramento City Councilor Mai Vang, a democratic socialist. Matsui is backed by the Democratic establishment, including the state party, Governor Gavin Newsom, both US senators and 37 members of California's congressional delegation. The outcome won't affect the balance of power in the House, but it could affect the makeup of a future Democratic majority. Several progressive or democratic socialist candidates have ousted mainstream or moderate Democrats in primaries this year, giving the left wing of the party significant momentum heading into a presidential election cycle in 2028.

item.title: OFRMO Summary
item.description: Gaza-Faute de fonds, le PAM réduit son aide à 500.000 Palestiniens
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Gaza-Faute de fonds, le PAM réduit son aide à 500.000 Palestiniens LE CAIRE/GAZA, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) des Nations Unies a déclaré lundi que le manque de financement l'obligeait à réduire considérablement son programme d'aide à Gaza, laissant ainsi environ 500.000 personnes sans aide alimentaire mensuelle sur un territoire où les deux tiers de la population restent en situation d'insécurité alimentaire aiguë. La police israélienne arrête 10 personnes en lien avec les diplomates européens attaqués par des colons en Cisjordanie occupée TEl AVIV , 19 octobre (Reuters) - La police israélienne a annoncé lundi avoir arrêté dix suspects dans le cadre de son enquête sur les incidents violents survenus ce week-end en Cisjordanie occupée, notamment des agressions menées par des colons juifs à la fois contre des diplomates européens et une journaliste du Washington Post. France: Macron refuse la démission du ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez PARIS, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Emmanuel Macron a rejeté la proposition de démission présentée par le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, à la suite des violences qui ont émaillé la mobilisation de ce week-end, a indiqué lundi l'Élysée. Brésil-Premier débat entre Bolsonaro et Lula, les attaques personnelles fusent BRASILIA, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro et le président sortant Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, qui s'affronteront lors du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil le 25 octobre, ont participé dimanche soir à un premier débat télévisé tendu lors duquel les attaques personnelles ont fusé. Nouvelle frappe russe sur Kyiv, une femme morte - maire KYIV, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Une frappe russe sur Kyiv a tué une femme et fait trois blessés dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi, a déclaré le maire de la capitale ukrainienne, précisant qu'une station de métro avait été touchée et un immeuble résidentiel de 25 étages endommagé. Canada-Un feu de prairie sur une base militaire en Alberta tue 4 personnes CALGARY, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Un incendie déclenché par un feu de broussailles a tué quatre soldats et fait 39 blessés, dont 19 se trouvent dans un état critique, sur une base d'entraînement de l'armée canadienne dans la province de l'Alberta, dans l'ouest du pays, ont déclaré dimanche soir les autorités locales. Trump dispose d'un délai pour se prononcer sur les sanctions contre la Russie, dit Rubio Le secrétaire d'Etat américain Marco Rubio a déclaré samedi que Donald Trump disposait d'un délai pouvant aller jusqu'à 60 jours pour évaluer l'impact économique des sanctions et des droits de douane liés à la Russie. L'Egypte prête à contribuer à la sécurité de l'Arabie saoudite 18 octobre (Reuters) - L'Egypte est prête à apporter à l'Arabie saoudite le soutien nécessaire à la défense de sa sécurité et de sa stabilité face aux attaques des Houthis, a déclaré dimanche la présidence égyptienne. Première apparition publique du pape depuis son opération pour un cancer du poumon CITE DU VATICAN, 18 octobre (Reuters) - Le pape Léon XIV a promis dimanche de reprendre progressivement ses fonctions à la tête de l'Eglise catholique lors de sa première apparition publique depuis son opération subie il y a cinq jours pour un cancer du poumon. Les USA ont repris le partage de renseignements avec l'Ukraine, dit Zelensky 18 octobre (Reuters) - Les États-Unis ont repris le partage de renseignements avec l'Ukraine pour l'aider à se défendre contre les attaques de missiles russes, a déclaré dimanche le président Volodimir Zelensky.
